title: Transperineal laser ablation for BPH-related LUTS: prospective evaluation of functional outcomes and predictors of treatment response.
abstract: To prospectively evaluate the clinical and functional outcomes of Transperineal Laser Ablation (TPLA) for men with bothersome Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms (LUTS) secondary to Benign Prostatic Obstruction (BPO). Consecutive patients treated with TPLA using the SoracteLite™ Echolaser system between January 2020 and March 2024 at a tertiary referral center were prospectively enrolled. Baseline prostate volume, International Prostate Symptom Score (IPSS), maximum flow rate (Qmax), and Male Sexual Health Questionnaire-Ejaculatory Dysfunction (MSHQ-EjD) scores were collected. Functional and patient-reported outcomes were assessed at 3, 6, and 12 months. Multivariable regression models were used to explore independent predictors of the 12-month change in Qmax and IPSS. A total of 178 patients were included. Median prostate volume was 60 mL (IQR 40-80), and 24.2% were receiving antiplatelet or anticoagulant therapy. Median operative time was 45 min (IQR 30-60), and no intraoperative complications occurred. At 12 months, median IPSS decreased from 18 to 6 (primary endpoint), Qmax increased from 10 to 14 mL/s, post-void residual volume decreased from 50 to 30 mL and MSHQ-EjD score increased from 7 to 15, while IIEF-5 remained stable; no patient reported loss of antegrade ejaculation. Retention-related events occurred in 26 patients (14.6%), mostly within the first 3 months; most reflected early failure of the trial without catheter, whereas acute urinary retention after recovery of spontaneous voiding occurred in seven patients (3.9%). Five men (2.8%) underwent subsequent disobstructive surgery, including two (1.1%) who never regained spontaneous voiding after TPLA (Clavien-Dindo IIIb). Despite α-blockers being permanently discontinued in most patients, 55 men (30.9%) required reintroduction during follow-up, although urinary functional outcomes remained comparable regardless of medication status. On multivariable analysis, prostate volume and energy delivered per milliliter of prostate volume were independently associated with both ΔQmax and ΔIPSS at 12 months, and baseline IPSS with ΔIPSS. In this prospective single-center series, TPLA provided significant relief of LUTS at 12 months, with a low rate of major complications and no reported loss of antegrade ejaculation. The association between energy delivered per milliliter of prostate volume and functional improvement is hypothesis-generating and warrants dedicated dose-response studies before it can inform treatment planning.

ADVANCE-FORSEE study protocol: Advanced video monitoring for early signalling of adverse events and optimal discharge planning in cardiac surgery patients.
abstract: Postoperative complications remain common after cardiac surgery, while manual nurse-led vital signs monitoring on post-cardiac surgery wards may delay their detection. Early recognition of clinical deterioration leading to complications is therefore essential to reduce post-surgery morbidity, and mortality. Conversely, personalised early discharge for patients with a fast and uneventful recovery may prevent unnecessarily delayed discharge and thereby free up hospital capacity. This study protocol describes the planned evaluation of the feasibility and acceptability of continuous video-based monitoring for early detection of postoperative deterioration as well as identification of uneventful recovery in cardiac surgery patients. This single-centre prospective observational study will include cardiac surgery patients admitted to the cardiothoracic surgery ward, with a target sample size of 300 patients. Video recordings will be made during postoperative ward stay and processed retrospectively to extract heart rate, arrhythmias, and respiration rate as well as contextual parameters (e.g., posture, movement and facial cues). These video-derived features will be used to train and evaluate machine-learning models for early detection of postoperative deterioration and assessment of discharge readiness. Patient enrolment is scheduled to start in November 2026 and is expected to be completed by November 2028. The first deterioration detection and discharge readiness models are expected by December 2028. The ADVANCE-FORSEE study was initiated to test the hypothesis that, by using video-based monitoring, we will be able to (1) mitigate the number and impact of postoperative adverse events and (2) identify patients with an uneventful recovery in an early stage. These insights may contribute to the development of tailored and individualised postoperative care pathways.

title: Digital Health Platform for Interinstitutional Perinatal Blood Dispatch in Rural Taiwan: 4-Year Implementation Study Using the RE-AIM Framework.
abstract: Postpartum hemorrhage is the leading direct cause of maternal mortality worldwide. In rural regions where obstetric clinics lack on-site transfusion capability, distance to the tertiary blood bank is a modifiable determinant of outcome. Existing electronic blood-ordering systems are confined to single-site hospital deployments; no peer-reviewed report describes an interinstitutional perinatal blood dispatch platform coordinating a tertiary blood bank with primary obstetric clinics. This study aims to describe the design, implementation, and RE-AIM (Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, and Maintenance) evaluation of a digital platform linking a tertiary blood bank with 4 community obstetric clinics in rural Taiwan over 4 years. We conducted an observational implementation evaluation at a tertiary referral center. Launched on November 1, 2021, the platform is a stand-alone web application coordinating ordering, identity and blood-type verification, and cold-chain dispatch across the blood bank and 4 affiliated clinics; it is not electronically integrated with the hospital blood-bank information system. Effectiveness was assessed against 2 prespecified service-level agreement (SLA) targets set by consensus before launch: routine dispatch ≥90% within 90 minutes and emergency dispatch ≥90% within 30 minutes. Reach, adoption, implementation, and maintenance were extracted from platform audit logs. Stakeholder satisfaction was measured using a 28-item service quality (SERVQUAL) instrument at 3 and 15 months postimplementation (clinic physicians, nurses, and allied staff). A continuous-improvement unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) delivery feasibility substudy (initiated in year 3) evaluated whole-blood stability across 4 red-cell storage time points over a 4-km corridor. The platform supported 252 dispatch episodes (38 emergency and 214 routine) from November 1, 2021, through August 31, 2026, and delivered 554 blood product units. Adoption reached 100% (4/4) of eligible clinics and all obstetric clinicians. The emergency SLA was met in 84.2% (32/38) of episodes and 100% in both 2025 and 2026 to date; median emergency turnaround was 28 (IQR 23-29) minutes. The routine SLA was met in 97.7% (209/214) of episodes; median routine turnaround was 72 (IQR 62-79) minutes. Zero serious transfusion-related adverse events were documented across all 252 episodes. SERVQUAL composite satisfaction rose from 4.65 (SD 0.53; n=32; Cronbach α=0.985) at 3 months to 5.00 (SD 0.01; n=38; α uninformative owing to ceiling effect) at 15 months. In the UAV substudy, preflight and postflight whole-blood parameters remained within similar ranges across all 4 storage days. An interinstitutional perinatal blood dispatch platform achieved universal clinic adoption, sustained prespecified SLA targets for emergency and routine dispatch, and was compatible with 0 serious transfusion-related adverse events across nearly 5 years of rural operation. Organizational-level digital health interventions in resource-constrained perinatal networks need not depend on full hospital-information-system integration while supporting sustained service quality; prespecified SLA frameworks plus audit-log analytics offer a transparent evaluation mechanism where randomized comparator designs are infeasible. UAV-delivery feasibility findings are preliminary.

title: The reduced hospital costs of periprosthetic joint infection patients with successful initial treatment : two-year estimations using activity-based costing.
abstract: This study aimed to 1) estimate the two-year hospital costs of treating periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) patients by outcomes of treatment success or treatment failure; 2) compare costs between patients with treatment success or treatment failure, stratified by PJI presentation and initial treatment type; and 3) estimate the cost burden for the study cohort and the projected Australian PJI cost burden of PJI patients by treatment success outcomes. A total of 212 hip and 287 knee patients from the Prosthetic joint Infection in Australia and New Zealand Observational (PIANO) study were included. Patients were grouped by treatment success outcomes, treatment type, and timing of PJI presentation (early acute, late acute, or chronic) at two-year follow-up. Hospital costs were calculated using activity-based costing. For hips, the mean cost of 67 patients with treatment failure was AUD $85,179 (SD 72,030), which was 1.44-fold higher than of 145 successfully treated patients ($59,234 (SD 45,581)). Of successfully treated hip patients, those who underwent additional surgeries ($70,257 (SD 38,481)) had 1.25-fold higher mean costs than patients with successful initial treatment ($56,238 (SD 42,929)). For knees, the mean cost of 133 patients with treatment failure ($89,073 (SD 64,707)) was 1.72-fold higher than 154 patients with successful treatment ($51,785 (SD 31,449)). Of successfully treated knee patients, those who underwent additional surgery ($85,326 (SD 44,885)) had 1.88-fold higher mean costs than patients with successful initial treatment ($45,284 (SD 23,286)). Treatment failure outcomes for patients initially treated with two-stage revision total hip arthroplasty, two-stage revision total knee arthroplasty, single-stage revision total knee arthroplasty, and extensive knee debridement, antibiotics, and implant retention (DAIR) cost 1.78, 1.94, 1.74, and 1.79-fold higher, respectively, compared with successfully treated patients with the same initial treatment (p < 0.05). At two-year follow-up, PJI patients with successful initial treatment had reduced hospital costs, highlighting the importance of strategies that aim to 'get it right the first time'. Patients with treatment failure account for approximately $131 million (51%) of the estimated $254 million annual Australian burden of hip and knee PJI.

title: Telehealth in military settings: policy challenges, lessons learned, and a framework for action - an integrative review with implications for health policy in Israel and beyond.
journal: Israel journal of health policy research
abstract: Background Military health systems must deliver care to dispersed, mobile and often hard-to-reach populations, and telehealth has become central to how they do so. Yet the evidence on military telehealth has rarely been synthesized with a view to the policy decisions that determine whether it is used appropriately, efficiently and effectively. Objective To integrate the evidence on telehealth in military settings worldwide, with particular attention to the Israel Defense Forces (IDF), in order to identify what policymakers need to know and to propose policies that specify what should be done, who should do it, and how. Methods Integrative review following the Whittemore and Knafl framework. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science and Google Scholar were searched for publications from 2010 to 2025, with earlier foundational sources, supplemented by NATO, governmental and institutional publications. Of 418 records identified, 47 sources were included; two further studies were added during peer review. Results Telehealth in military settings consistently improves access to specialist care, reduces unnecessary travel and medical evacuations, sustains care during crises such as the COVID-19 pandemic and armed conflict, and delivers behavioral health treatment with outcomes comparable to in-person care. Its limits are equally consistent: unsuitability for some clinical situations, fragile connectivity, stringent cybersecurity requirements, regulatory gaps, insufficient training, and uneven uptake across groups. In Israel, the IDF has established base-located telemedicine complexes and expanded digital mental health services amid a growing mental health burden since October 7, 2023, but published data on utilization and outcomes are scarce and the regulatory framework for military telehealth is incomplete. Conclusions The main obstacles to military telehealth are now organizational and regulatory rather than technological. We propose seven policies, each with responsible actors and implementation steps: clinical appropriateness guidelines; a legal framework for telehealth that explicitly covers military care; risk-tiered cybersecurity certification; evaluated investment in remote-examination technologies; mandatory telehealth competency training; equity-oriented deployment with priority for telemental health; and a military telehealth data and surge-preparedness system. These policies are also relevant to civilian health systems. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: CORONARY ARTERY DISEASE PATIENTS UNDERGOING PERCUTANEOUS CORONARY INTERVENTION GUIDED BY QUANTITATIVE FLOW RATIO: A CORRELATION STUDY
journal: Journal of Pharmaceutical and Medical Research
abstract: To investigate the differences in clinical baseline, imaging parameters and laboratory indicators between quantitative flow fraction (QFR)≤0.80 and QFR>0.80 in patients with coronary heart disease who make decisions on percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) guided by QFR, and to analyze the correlation between QFR and various variables. A total of 97 patients with coronary heart disease were obtained by matching 111 patients in the QFR report database of our hospital with 111 discharge records according to patient ID. According to the preoperative target vessel QFR, the patients were divided into QFR≤0.80 group (n=37, with the indication of ischemic intervention) and QFR>0.80 group (n=60, without the indication of intervention, without PCI Treatment). Continuous variables were expressed as median [interquartile range], Mann Whitney U test was used for comparison between groups, χ²or Fisher exact test was used for categorical variables, and Spearman rank correlation was used for correlation. The preoperative QFR of 97 patients was 0.77 ± 0.20. The clinical baseline was balanced between the two groups. At the same time, the anatomic load was heavier in the QFR≤0.80 group, while there was no difference in the reference lumen diameter (P=0.664). There was no statistically significant difference in laboratory indexes between the two groups. In the QFR≤0.80 group, the patients were grouped according to the QFR tertile (threshold p33=0.470, p67=0.670). The diameter stenosis rate and area stenosis rate in the lower tertile group were significantly higher than those in the upper tertile group (p=0.023, p=0.022). The PCI planning gainΔQFR (software simulation value) increased gradiently (p<0.001). QFR was negatively correlated with maximum diameter stenosis rate (r= − 0.800) and maximum area stenosis rate (r= − 0.799), and positively correlated with MLD (r=+0.567) (all p<0.001). In the real-world population in which QFR guides treatment decisions, the clinical background of QFR ≤0.80 and QFR>0.80 lesions is balanced and the anatomical load is significantly different. Preoperative QFR level is closely related to anatomic load and PCI planning gain, and can be used as a reference index for treatment decision-making and preoperative risk assessment.

title: Cancer patient pathways and care coordination in Kuwait: an exploratory process mining study using linked health data
abstract: Background: The rising incidence and complexity of cancer treatment increase the need to understand care delivered across specialties and facilities. Evidence on cancer pathways remains limited in settings with fragmented health data. This study evaluated the feasibility of linking multiple healthcare data sources for process mining and described breast and colorectal cancer pathways in Kuwait.Methods: In this retrospective cohort study, we linked two administrative datasets: patient records from the Kuwait Cancer Control Center (KCCC) Electronic Health Record (EHR) system covering 2015 through the first quarter of 2023, and national hospital discharge data from the Ministry of Health (MOH) for 2015, 2016, 2019 and 2020. Fifty patients were purposively selected, 25 with breast cancer and 25 with colorectal cancer. The linked event log comprised 3,334 activity records and was examined using process discovery, event classification and Sankey visualization.Results: Colorectal cancer patients recorded more clinic visits per week than breast cancer patients (0.31 vs. 0.23, p<0.05) and more diagnostic events per patient (26.0 vs. 12.2, p<0.05), driven by laboratory and radiology testing. Breast cancer patients recorded more radiation oncology activity (p<0.05). Average captured journey length did not differ (51.4 vs. 49.5 months, p = 0.726). Medical oncology appeared in 92% of breast and 100% of colorectal cancer journeys. General hospitals accounted for 24 of 101 (24%) colorectal hospitalizations, compared with 8 of 74 (11%) breast cancer hospitalizations.Conclusions: Linking MOH discharge data with KCCC EHR records was feasible and made multi-facility cancer trajectories visible. The observed pathway differences are hypothesis-generating and identify priorities for larger, representative studies and for more complete, standardized event capture.

An Early Presentation of Taxane and Anti-human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor 2 (Anti-HER2)-Induced Pneumonitis: A Case Report
abstract: Pulmonary toxicity is a rare but potentially life-threatening complication of taxane-based chemotherapy combined with anti-human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) therapy and may be difficult to distinguish from infection in immunocompromised patients. We report the case of a 53-year-old woman with stage III, HER2-positive, estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer who developed acute hypoxemic respiratory failure eight days after receiving paclitaxel, trastuzumab, and pertuzumab. Chest computed tomography revealed bilateral scattered ground-glass opacities. Initial empirical antimicrobial treatment targeting opportunistic infections, including Pneumocystis jirovecii and cytomegalovirus, produced no clinical improvement. Microbiological investigations were negative, while bronchoalveolar lavage cytology revealed marked lymphocytic and neutrophilic alveolitis without malignant cells. Drug-induced pneumonitis associated with the taxane-anti-HER2 combination was suspected, and prednisolone at 1 mg/kg/day was initiated, followed by progressive respiratory improvement and discontinuation of high-flow oxygen therapy. The patient was subsequently discharged under a home hospitalization program and discontinued oxygen therapy one week later. Given the severity of the suspected drug-induced pneumonitis, neoadjuvant treatment was discontinued and subsequent surgery revealed a pathological complete response. This case highlights the importance of considering treatment-related pneumonitis in patients presenting with acute respiratory deterioration shortly after taxane and anti-HER2 therapy. Diagnosis requires an integrated assessment of treatment chronology, imaging, microbiological findings, and clinical response. Although the temporal relationship suggests treatment-associated pulmonary toxicity, the individual contribution of paclitaxel, trastuzumab, and pertuzumab cannot be established. Early recognition and timely corticosteroid treatment are essential in severe cases, and hospital-at-home programs can contribute to early hospital discharge.

title: Telehealth as an alternative pathway for low-acuity acute care: clinical appropriateness, economic value, patient acceptance, and public-health implications
abstract: The rapid expansion of telehealth has created opportunities to reconsider how patients with low-acuity acute conditions access care and whether virtual services can reduce reliance on emergency departments (EDs). This narrative review evaluates the role of telehealth as an alternative acute-care pathway, integrating evidence on clinical appropriateness, healthcare utilization, economic outcomes, access and equity, safety and quality, and patient acceptance. Available evidence indicates that telehealth can safely resolve selected low-acuity conditions and facilitate triage for others, but the proportion of ED encounters that can realistically be substituted by virtual care is substantially smaller than retrospective estimates of non-emergent ED use suggest. Economic studies generally demonstrate lower resource utilization and patient-level costs for virtual care, although evidence for healthcare-system cost savings remains heterogeneous and depends on whether telehealth genuinely substitutes for higher-cost care rather than generating additional or duplicative encounters. Similarly, broad telehealth expansion does not consistently reduce ED utilization; targeted models positioned at the point of acute-care decision-making appear more promising for achieving meaningful substitution. Population-level Medicare data demonstrate both the rapid expansion of telemedicine and persistent differences in utilization across demographic and geographic groups, underscoring the importance of digital access and health equity. Patient behavior represents an additional determinant of effectiveness: awareness, perceived symptom severity, trust in virtual assessment, convenience, cost, prior experience, and clinician recommendation influence willingness to select telehealth for acute symptoms. Taken together, the evidence supports an integrated model in which telehealth serves not as a universal replacement for emergency care but as an accessible clinical entry point that directs patients toward virtual resolution, targeted in-person evaluation, or emergency escalation based on clinical need. Public-health strategies should therefore prioritize appropriate triage, equitable access, patient trust and awareness, interoperable care pathways, and episode-level outcomes rather than telehealth volume or ED avoidance alone.

title: The level of diabetes knowledge and associated factors among Chinese patients with type 2 diabetes in Hong Kong primary care settings
abstract: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is a chronic illness with major global impact on healthcare systems and a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in Hong Kong. Adequate DM knowledge is crucial for an effective management and complication prevention, yet recent local data are lacking. This study aimed to find out the proportion of Chinese adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) attending public family medicine clinics(FMCs) who have adequate and inadequate DM knowledge, and to explore sociodemographic and clinical parameters associated with DM knowledge adequacy. This was a cross-sectional study conducted in three FMCs from 1st August 2024 to 28th February 2025. DM knowledge was measured using the validated 24-item Diabetes Knowledge Questionnaire(DKQ-24), patients with 75% or more correct responses (18 or more out of 24 items) were considered to have an adequate knowledge. Of 410 participants invited, 380 (92.7%) were included in the analysis. Only 18.9% demonstrated adequate DM knowledge (mean DKQ-24 score: 13.3, SD 4.1). Attending a district health centre (DHC) DM management programme was strongly associated with adequate DM knowledge (adjusted OR 4.320; 95% CI: 2.086–8.946; adjusted p < 0.001)), whereas being overweight/obese was inversely associated with adequate knowledge (adjusted OR 0.378 ; 95% CI: 0.210–0.680; adjusted p = 0.001). These findings highlighted the attendance at the DHC DM management programme was independently associated with higher odds of adequate diabetes knowledge and primary care physicians could consider expanding access, particularly for overweight/obese patients. Understanding the associated factors of DM knowledge adequacy would facilitate the development of a more structured and culturally relevant DM health education programme.

title: Two-year outcomes from the HyPORT-BC study: hypofractionated radiotherapy for Japanese breast cancer patients after surgery
abstract: Purpose: International guidelines now prefer hypofractionated radiotherapy for breast cancer, yet prospective data for Japanese patients remain limited. In our prospective observational study of hypofractionated radiotherapy for Japanese breast cancer patients (HyPORT-BC), acute adverse events were found to be within an acceptable range. Herein, we report the 2-year follow-up data. Materials and Methods: Between January and December 2023, 123 Japanese patients were enrolled: 81 received moderately hypofractionated radiotherapy (42.5 Gy/16 fractions) including the supraclavicular lymph node region (cohort M), and 42 received ultra-hypofractionated radiotherapy (26 Gy/5 fractions) for the conserved breast (cohort U). For endpoints, overall survival (OS), relapse-free survival (RFS), ipsilateral breast relapse-free survival (IBRS), locoregional relapse-free survival (LRFS), late adverse events (Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events version 5.0), and cosmetic deterioration were evaluated. Results: At a median follow-up of 28.8 months for cohort M and 25.2 months for cohort U, the 2-year OS, RFS, IBRS, and LRFS were 96.2%, 91.3%, 100%, and 95.0% for cohort M, and 97.0%, 94.5%, 97.0%, and 97.0% for cohort U, respectively. The proportion of evaluable patients with grade ≥2 late adverse events (AEs) at the 24-month assessment was 9.1% in cohort M, whereas no grade ≥2 late AEs were observed in cohort U. Regarding cosmetic outcomes, the proportion of patients who showed any worsening from baseline was 12.5% in cohort M and 20.0% in cohort U. Conclusion: As preliminary descriptive findings, both moderately hypofractionated and ultra-hypofractionated radiotherapy showed suggest acceptable 2-year efficacy and toxicity with encouraging early cosmetic preservation in Japanese patients.

title: Voices from the frontline: a qualitative exploration of practice dilemmas and support needs among anesthesia intensive care unit nurses in China
abstract: Background Anesthesia intensive care units (AICUs) provide continuous monitoring and early intervention for high-risk postoperative patients. The development of AICUs and standardization of nursing care have received increasing attention in China. However, little is known about AICU nurses’ work experiences and support needs. Understanding their experiences may inform improvements in nursing management within this emerging care setting. Objective To explore the practice dilemmas and support needs of AICU nurses in China. Methods A descriptive qualitative study was conducted between May and June 2025. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 18 AICU nurses from eight tertiary hospitals in China. Data were analyzed using thematic analysis, with the Job Demands–Resources (JD-R) model serving as an interpretive framework. Results Three themes were identified. The first theme, clinical competence and care burden dilemmas, encompassed inadequate nurse staffing, a lack of standardized nursing documentation, and gaps in integrated clinical competencies. The second theme, internal workflow and teamwork dilemmas, included unclear admission and transfer-out criteria, non-standardized night-shift workflows, and limited team stability. The third theme, interdepartmental integration and organizational recognition dilemmas, involved difficulties in coordinating patient flow, unclear organizational positioning of the AICU, and insufficient organizational recognition. Collectively, these findings indicate a mismatch between job demands and available job resources across clinical, team, and organizational levels. Conclusion The practice dilemmas experienced by AICU nurses do not arise from a single factor. Instead, they reflect mismatches between job demands and job resources at multiple levels. Nursing leaders could provide coordinated support through appropriate staffing, professional development, standardized workflows, team stability, and clear organizational positioning of the AICU.

title: Cerebral Sinovenous Thrombosis: A Pediatric Tertiary Center Case Series From the United Arab Emirates (UAE)
abstract: Background: Cerebral sinovenous thrombosis (CSVT) is a rare but significant cause of pediatric morbidity and mortality, with management strategies often extrapolated from adult data due to a paucity of pediatric‑specific evidence. This study aims to characterize the clinical presentations, etiological profiles, neuroimaging findings, therapeutic approaches, and outcomes of pediatric CSVT at a single pediatric tertiary center in the UAE, making this the first pediatric case series from the region. Methods: A retrospective case series was conducted at Al Jalila Children's Hospital, Dubai, including all children under 18 years with radiologically confirmed CSVT between 2015 and 2025. Data on demographics, clinical features, risk factors, imaging, treatment, and outcomes were collected. Results: Thirteen children (median age: 6 years, 54% male) were identified. Trauma was the predominant etiology (46%), followed by infection (38%). Headache (82%) and vomiting (69%) were the most common symptoms; cranial nerve involvement occurred in 46%, and seizures in 31%. The sigmoid sinus was the most frequently involved site (62%), and more than half of the patients (54%) had more than one sinus involved. Anticoagulation was administered to 62% of patients and was well tolerated. Complete recanalization was demonstrated in 100% of the cohort with follow-up imaging (n=8), including 6 who received anticoagulation and 2 who underwent conservative management without anticoagulation. Favorable neurological outcome (modified Rankin Scale: 0-2) was observed in 89% of patients with available follow-up data (8 of 9; excluding the deceased patient). One remaining patient experienced an unfavorable outcome characterized by focal symptomatic epilepsy and global developmental delay, while the deceased patient succumbed during the initial hospitalization due to systemic sepsis and uncontrolled intracranial hypertension. Conclusions: Pediatric CSVT represents a diagnostic and therapeutic challenge. Awareness is especially important in children with risk factors such as head and neck infections, trauma, and anemia. Anticoagulation is both safe and effective for restoring venous flow, though a high rate of recanalization can be achieved with conservative management. Clinicians should routinely include venography in the neuroimaging workup of children with risk factors presenting with a combination of headache, vomiting, seizures, and cranial nerve palsies, and consider anticoagulation for all symptomatic patients lacking major intracranial hemorrhage to mitigate acute CSVT complications, shorten the course of illness, and optimize outcomes.

title: Decannulation and noninvasive ventilation: the respiratory support loop
abstract: Liberation from an artificial airway through decannulation and liberation from mechanical ventilatory support are fundamentally distinct clinical objectives that have historically been conflated. In complex critical care populations, including patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), obesity hypoventilation syndrome, neuromuscular diseases, high cervical spinal cord injury, and stroke, ventilatory muscle pump failure often persists beyond the need for an invasive airway. Traditional sequential weaning pathways, progressing from invasive mechanical ventilation to a spontaneous breathing trial, decannulation, and complete liberation, may unnecessarily prolong tracheostomy dependence, increase hospital-acquired pulmonary infections, impair swallowing, and delay the restoration of speech. This review introduces the Respiratory Support Loop (RSL), a cyclical model integrating non-invasive ventilation (NIV) as an active bridging strategy between liberation from invasive ventilation and decannulation. Once upper airway patency, swallowing safety and effective cough clearance have been established, decannulation can proceed while NIV supports respiratory muscle function during periods of increased demand, particularly overnight. We propose a multidomain readiness assessment covering six physiological domains: neurological status; upper airway anatomy; swallowing safety; cough effectiveness; respiratory muscle strength; and gas exchange. The review presents practical protocols for NIV with a downsized, capped tracheostomy tube in situ, the management of peristomal air leakage and phenotype-specific weaning pathways. The review incorporates a critical appraisal of the evidence using GRADE certainty ratings, Cochrane systematic reviews and the Newcastle–Ottawa Scale (NOS) for cohort studies. The evidence reviewed supports the use of high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) as a bridging strategy and targeted respiratory muscle training. However, it should be noted that the evidence for sequential NIV-supported weaning is predominantly observational. Decannulation decisions should be based on multidimensional clinical readiness rather than on capping trials or oxygenation measurements in isolation. Persistent compensated hypercapnia should not be considered an absolute contraindication to decannulation. Every patient discharged through this pathway should have a clearly defined, phenotype-specific plan for long-term respiratory support.

title: Diagnostic yield and clinical impact of whole-genome sequencing in neonates with congenital heart disease in the cardiac intensive care unit
abstract: Introduction Congenital heart defects (CHD) are a common congenital anomaly and a leading cause of neonatal mortality. Even in ostensibly isolated cases, genetic testing can reveal monogenic causes of isolated CHD or identify syndromic conditions before additional features become clinically apparent. A timely and accurate genetic diagnosis can inform medical management and surveillance, reduce the need for unnecessary investigations, and offer families valuable information about prognosis, recurrence risk, and anticipatory guidance. In September of 2023, Primary Children's Hospital introduced a universal genetic testing protocol that implemented whole genome sequencing for all neonates admitted to the cardiac intensive care unit (CICU) undergoing cardiac surgery before 30 days of life to increase the number of patients who receive a timely genetic diagnosis and improve clinical care. Methods We conducted retrospective chart review of patients who underwent whole genome sequencing (WGS) under the new universal genetic testing protocol at Primary Children's Hospital from its initiation in September 2023 to February 2026. Results During the study period, 217 neonates with CHD underwent WGS through the protocol. Of these patients, 23 (10.6%) received a genetic diagnosis that was causative of their CHD. Eleven of these 23 patients (48%) had no major extracardiac features at the time testing was ordered. Twenty patients received a diagnosis of a syndromic condition and three received a diagnosis of a non-syndromic condition. All syndromic patients received additional referrals to specialists following their new diagnosis, and six families had genetic testing results that were incorporated into decisions regarding continuation of care. An additional 19 patients (8.8%) received WGS results that were clinically relevant but non-diagnostic for their CHD, including partial diagnoses, secondary findings, and carrier status. In total, 19.4% of patients (n =42) had clinically relevant variants identified on their WGS. Discussion Universal WGS in neonates with CHD undergoing cardiac surgery identified a causative genetic diagnosis in 10.6% of patients, including nearly half who lacked major extracardiac features at the time of testing. An additional 8.8% had clinically relevant findings that, while not diagnostic of their CHD, may provide important information for patient care and family counseling.

title: Evaluating Human and AI-Based Triage Performance in the Emergency Department: Real-World Cohort Study
abstract: Background Emergency departments (EDs) depend on rapid, reliable triage for patient safety and flow. The Manchester Triage System (MTS) is widely implemented but exhibits known interrater variability. Large language models (LLMs) have emerged as potential decision-support tools for triage and early assessment, yet real-world comparative evaluations remain scarce. Objective This study aimed to compare clinician and LLM performance on ED triage accuracy, specialty assignment, diagnostic recommendations, and admission prediction in a real-world cohort. Methods In a retrospective cohort study, 305 walk-in ED encounters at a German tertiary-care hospital were analyzed. A nurse performed real-time MTS-assessment and initial specialty assignment at presentation. Each anonymized case was independently evaluated by 4 physicians and 12 LLMs from 4 providers (OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, and Mistral). Triage agreement was assessed against 2 reference standards: a consensus human label (ground-truth 1 [GT1]) and real-time nurse-assigned MTS-triage (ground-truth 2 [GT2]). For human raters, a leave-one-out variant of GT1 (LOO-GT1) assessed incorporation bias. The primary statistic was quadratic-weighted Cohen κ (unweighted κ reported alongside). Secondary outcomes were directional triage errors (over- or undertriage, |Δ|≤1), specialty top-1 accuracy, per-case precision, recall, F 1 -score of recommended diagnostics, and admission prediction (sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value [PPV], and negative predictive value [NPV]). Results Median age was 45 (IQR 31‐62) years; 188 (61.6%) patients were male; admission rate was 20.1% (56/278). Against GT1, human-rater (physicians and nurse) accuracy ranged 0.59‐0.83 (quadratic-weighted κ 0.60‐0.88; unweighted κ 0.35‐0.74), and LLM accuracy 0.35‐0.70 (quadratic-weighted κ 0.46‐0.72; unweighted κ 0.11‐0.53). Under LOO-GT1, human-rater weighted κ fell to 0.48‐0.81. Only 1 clinician (Doctor 1, weighted κ 0.81) retained agreement clearly above any LLM, while 3 LLMs (Gemini-3.5-flash=0.72, GPT-5.5=0.69, and GPT-5=0.66) exceeded the LOO-corrected agreement of the remaining 4 human raters. One-off agreement exceeded 86% for all raters and models. Vs GT1, overtriage ranged 6%‐56% and undertriage 6%‐36%. Vs GT2, corresponding ranges were 11%‐62% and 5%‐30%. Against the study specialty reference, physician specialty-assignment accuracy ranged 0.88‐0.93 and LLM accuracy 0.62‐0.80. Against the operational triage-pathway specialty assignment, the corresponding ranges were 0.81‐0.82 and 0.57‐0.75. Model diagnostic recommendation F 1 -scores ranged 0.55‐0.69. Admission prediction demonstrated high sensitivity (0.73‐0.95) and NPV (0.90‐0.96), but modest PPV (0.25‐0.41). Conclusions In a real-world ED cohort, 1 clinician (Doctor 1, a specialist physician) had the highest urgency agreement point estimate under both GT1 and LOO-GT1. Under LOO-GT1, 3 contemporary LLMs reached agreement that exceeded that of the other 4 clinicians. For specialty assignment, all clinicians remained clearly ahead of the best LLM. LLMs showed strong sensitivity and high NPV for admission prediction, but modest PPV precludes autonomous use. Because both reference standards are empirical rather than outcome-anchored gold standards, findings represent agreement against expert consensus and routine practice rather than an absolute correctness benchmark, and support a complementary, human-in-the-loop role for LLM-based decision-support in ED triage and early assessment.

title: Peribulbar versus topical anesthesia for pain during panretinal photocoagulation in proliferative diabetic retinopathy: a randomized controlled trial
abstract: Purpose To compare pain control with peribulbar anesthesia versus topical tetracaine alone during panretinal photocoagulation (PRP) in patients with proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR), and to assess its safety. Methods In this single-center, prospective, within-person, randomized, controlled superiority trial at a tertiary eye hospital in Mexico City, adults with PDR scheduled for their first PRP session were enrolled. Using block randomization, one eye of each patient was assigned to peribulbar anesthesia (1.5 mL of 2% lidocaine and 1.5 mL 0.5% bupivacaine) and the fellow eye to topical 5% tetracaine with a sham injection; both eyes were treated in the same session. Patients were masked to allocation; the outcome assessor was not. The primary outcome was pain on the numerical rating scale (NRS) at 1, 5, 10, and 15 minutes during PRP. Secondary outcomes were heart rate, respiratory rate, blood pressure and SpO2 at the same time points, and the presence of adverse events. Results Fifty patients (100 eyes) were randomized, and all 50 eyes in each group were analyzed. Peribulbar anesthesia produced significantly lower median pain scores: 3 vs. 4.5 at 1 minute (P = 0.01), 4 vs. 6 at 5 minutes (P = 0.01), and 6 vs. 7.5 at 15 minutes (P < 0.01), but not at 10 minutes (6 vs 7; P = 0.05). Additionally, respiratory rate dispersion was lower in this group at 15 minutes: 18 (16–18) vs. 18 (18–20) (P < 0.01). Heart rate, blood pressure, and SpO2 did not differ between groups. No anesthesia-related complications occurred; two patients had hypotension and one vomited during PRP of the control eye. Conclusion Our findings suggest that peribulbar anesthesia using lidocaine and bupivacaine significantly reduced pain during PRP compared with topical anesthesia alone, with no anesthesia-related complications observed. Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07640256, 2026-06-01, retrospectively registered. Funding: none.

title: Etiological Paradigm Shift, Sentinel Ocular Presentations, and Visual Recovery Dynamics in HIV-Associated Uveitis: A Retrospective Cohort Study at an Academic Referral Center in West Sumatra, Indonesia
journal: Open Access Indonesian Journal of Medical Reviews
abstract: Background: Uveitis frequently serves as the critical sentinel clinical manifestation unmasking occult Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) infection. In the contemporary combination antiretroviral therapy (cART) era, shifting epidemiology has transformed opportunistic intraocular infections. Objective: To evaluate the sociodemographic profile, CD4+ immunological status, anatomical phenotypes (SUN criteria), infectious etiologies, and visual acuity outcomes in HIV-infected patients presenting with active uveitis. Methods: A retrospective cohort study was conducted at Universitas Andalas Hospital, Padang, Indonesia (February 2023–August 2026), reviewing consecutive HIV patients presenting with active uveitis. Ophthalmic assessments included best-corrected visual acuity (LogMAR), slit-lamp biomicroscopy, funduscopy, ultrasonography, and serology. Visual changes post-targeted therapy were analyzed using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Result: Seventeen patients (34 eyes) were enrolled, demonstrating striking male predominance (94.1%) with a mean age of 33.1 ± 7.6 years. Crucially, 82.4% (n = 14) were newly diagnosed with HIV at ocular presentation. Panuveitis was the predominant phenotype (70.6%), presenting bilaterally in 52.9%. Ocular syphilis (Treponema pallidum) emerged as the leading etiology (82.4%), followed by cytomegalovirus retinitis (11.8%). Post-therapy, the legal blindness rate (< 20/400) halved from 35.3% to 17.6%. Mean visual acuity improved from LogMAR 1.00 ± 0.91 to 0.74 ± 0.87 (p = 0.055). Overall, 41.2% of eyes improved, 50.0% remained stable, and 8.8% deteriorated due to irreversible macular scarring. Conclusion: Severe uveitis, particularly syphilitic panuveitis, represents an indispensable sentinel marker for occult HIV in young males. Routine reflex dual-screening for HIV and syphilis is strongly recommended in atypical uveitis, as prompt targeted therapy achieves substantial functional visual salvage.

title: Real-world value based healthcare assessment of DIP payment for acute myocardial infarction in China: a multicenter retrospective cohort study
abstract: This study aimed to construct an exploratory, real-world framework to evaluate how Acute Myocardial Infarction (AMI) Diagnosis–Intervention Packet (DIP) reimbursement benchmarks align with clinical outcomes. Using electronic medical records from 32 tertiary public hospitals in China, we applied Generalized Estimating Equations with Firth penalized logistic regression to estimate risk-adjusted probabilities for in-hospital death and 30-day unplanned readmission in DIP-4215. We then constructed bivariate quality-cost models using segmented regression and restricted cubic splines (RCS) to explore potential value-based payment thresholds and ranges. We observed a “J-shaped” association between cost and quality in DIP-4215. The current payment (7,482.55 CNY) fell within the estimated value-based cost range for in-hospital death, but not for 30-day unplanned readmission. Furthermore, it did not fall within the overlapping value-based intervals when both outcomes were considered jointly. These exploratory findings highlight the methodological challenges and potential of using real-world data for value-based payment evaluation, demonstrating that while readmission exhibits a robust J-shaped cost-outcome association, mortality gradients are highly susceptible to death-truncated cost.

title: Precision hemodynamic resuscitation in septic shock: a clinician-in-the-loop state-test-response framework
abstract: Septic shock is hemodynamically heterogeneous, yet bedside resuscitation is often organized around population targets. This Review focuses on adult intensive care unit (ICU) patients with established septic shock after immediate rescue has begun and serial physiological reassessment is feasible. Current guidelines provide essential initial anchors for fluid, pressure, perfusion and vasoactive therapy, but do not specify how discordant signals should be integrated once initial rescue is underway. We propose a clinician-in-the-loop sequence: confirm current treatment need → identify the actionable mechanism(s) → select a time-limited therapeutic test with a prespecified response window and harm limits → measure response → maintain, stop or switch. Unlike frameworks centered primarily on targets or fluid phases, this approach explicitly separates indication, physiological eligibility and treatment response, and assumes that mixed states are common. We describe standardized capillary refill time (CRT) measurement, contextual interpretation of lactate, real-time flow assessment for preload responsiveness, graded fluid-tolerance constraints, and ICU-specific operational examples with evidence levels identified as guideline-supported, trial-derived, common evidence-supported or pragmatic. ANDROMEDA-SHOCK-2 is used as an example of multicomponent physiological testing rather than proof of any individual component. Neutral fluid and vasopressor-prioritization trials are interpreted according to setting, timing, treatment separation and adverse events. The next research step is prospective validation of state assignment, response thresholds and clinician-in-the-loop decision rules against patient-centered outcomes.
