ATF7 coordinates early transcriptional priming to enable direct cardiac reprogramming
abstract: Direct cardiac reprogramming relies on the canonical transcription factor cocktail MEF2C, GATA4, and TBX5 (MGT), yet successful lineage conversion requires additional non-cocktail regulators that coordinate the chromatin and transcriptional transitions underlying fibroblast-to-cardiomyocyte conversion. Here, we identify Activating Transcription Factor 7 (ATF7) as a critical supporting factor that enables efficient direct cardiac reprogramming. Loss-of-function studies in primary murine cardiac fibroblasts demonstrate that Atf7 knockdown markedly reduces MGT-mediated reprogramming efficiency, with the strongest impairment occurring when Atf7 is depleted during the early priming window of days 0-3. Transcriptomic profiling reveals that Atf7 knockdown disrupts the induction of cardiomyocyte gene programs while restoring expression of fibroblast- and extracellular-matrix-associated pathways, shifting the global expression profile toward a non-reprogrammed state. CUT&RUN mapping across days 0, 3, and 6 of reprogramming shows that ATF7 binds dynamically to lineage-relevant regulatory regions, engaging cardiac loci-including those encoding Gata4 and Tbx5-early in reprogramming, and increasingly occupying fibroblast-associated loci at later stages. Integration of ATF7 binding sites with published single-cell chromatin accessibility data identifies substantial overlap with iCM-enriched regulatory signatures, particularly at day 3, highlighting this stage as a critical node of ATF7 activity. Together, these findings reveal that ATF7 executes a bifunctional regulatory role by simultaneously promoting cardiomyocyte-specific gene activation and repressing fibroblast-associated transcriptional networks. Our study establishes ATF7 as a previously unrecognized regulatory component necessary for efficient MGT-driven cardiac reprogramming and provides a preliminary mechanistic framework for its dual lineage-modulating functions.

title: Experiences of nurses providing mental health care to suicidal adolescents in a public psychiatric hospital
abstract: Suicide-related behaviour, including suicidal ideation, planning, and suicide attempts, is a significant cause of death worldwide, particularly among adolescents. This study explored and described the experiences of nurses providing mental healthcare to adolescents with suicidal behaviour and the support that can be provided to them. ​The study was conducted in the adolescent ward of a public psychiatric hospital in the Western Cape, South Africa, this study employed a descriptive qualitative research design. Purposive sampling was used to recruit 11 participants (registered nurses, enrolled nurses, and enrolled nursing assistants) for semi-structured interviews, with data saturation guiding the final sample size. Data were analysed using thematic analysis, while trustworthiness was ensured through established measures of dependability, transferability, credibility, and confirmability. Ethical approval was obtained from the relevant authorities prior to commencing the study. Four themes emerged from the data, which are: (1) Caring for suicidal adolescents is challenging. (2) Caring for suicidal adolescents can be rewarding. (3) Need for emotional and/or psychological support. (4) Need for organisational support. This study highlighted the emotional and physical demands associated with caring for adolescents exhibiting suicidal behaviour in a South African public psychiatric hospital and identified ways to support mental health nurses in fulfilling their responsibilities. The findings indicate that healthcare organisations should implement structured post-incident debriefing, provide accessible psychological support, offer adolescent-specific suicide-care training, ensure adequate staffing, and promote supportive, non-punitive managerial practices. Strengthening adolescent mental health services and ensuring continuity of care following discharge are also necessary to reduce the pressures experienced by both nurses and adolescents. These measures may enhance nurses’ well-being and improve the quality and continuity of care provided to adolescents experiencing suicidal behaviour. Not applicable.

title: Patient-Specific Three-Dimensional Reconstruction for Planning Robot-Assisted Radical Prostatectomy: Console Time and Positive Surgical Margins in a Multicenter Cohort
authors: Ana Luisa Bastos Andrade Benevidesdos Reis
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the association between patient-specific three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction for robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) planning and perioperative and early oncologic outcomes. Methods This ambispective, two-center study included 160 patients undergoing RARP between January 2024 and September 2026: 80 with 3D reconstruction derived from multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging and 80 controls. Positive surgical margin status was the primary outcome. Console time and hospital stay were secondary outcomes. Multivariable analyses assessed adjusted associations. Results Positive surgical margins occurred in 17.5% of the 3D group and 20.0% of controls (p = 0.685). The adjusted odds ratio was 0.86 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.37–2.02; p = 0.735). Median console time was 82.0 versus 95.5 minutes (p < 0.001), with an adjusted difference of − 15.83 minutes (95% CI − 24.63 to − 7.04; p < 0.001), including adjustment for lymphadenectomy. Among patients without lymphadenectomy, the adjusted difference was − 15.93 minutes (95% CI − 28.18 to − 3.67; p = 0.012). Median hospital stay was 24 hours in both groups; adjusted stay was 4.96 hours longer with 3D reconstruction (95% CI 0.64–9.28; p = 0.025). Conclusion 3D reconstruction for RARP planning was associated with shorter console time, with no demonstrable difference in positive surgical margins. These observational findings suggest potential operative efficiency benefits; prospective randomized studies are needed to establish clinical and oncologic impact.

title: Diagnostic Performance of the Eustachian Tube Dysfunction Questionnaire-7 (ETDQ-7) in Predicting Objective Eustachian Tube Patency Among Patients with Chronic Rhinosinusitis: A Cross-Sectional Analytical Study at a Tertiary Referral Hospital in Bali, Indonesia
journal: Open Access Indonesian Journal of Medical Reviews
abstract: Background: Chronic rhinosinusitis (CRS) can extend to the tubal orifice and cause Eustachian tube dysfunction. Concordance between ETDQ-7 symptoms and objective tubal patency in CRS remains uncertain. Objective: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of ETDQ-7 for objective tubal patency impairment in adults with CRS in Bali, Indonesia. Methods: This analytical cross-sectional study enrolled 42 consecutive adults with CRS at a tertiary hospital from January to March 2026. ETDQ-7 scores ≥14.5 were considered abnormal. Tubal patency was assessed by acoustic impedance tympanometry. Chi-square testing, Spearman correlation, and multivariable logistic regression were performed. Result: Mean age was 38.9 ± 11.6 years; 57.1% were female. Abnormal ETDQ-7 scores occurred in 24 patients (57.1%), and objective impairment occurred in 26 (61.9%). Impairment was more frequent with abnormal than normal ETDQ-7 scores (83.3% vs 33.3%, p = 0.002). Scores correlated with impaired patency (r = 0.58, p < 0.001). Abnormal ETDQ-7 independently predicted impairment (adjusted OR 7.84, 95% CI 1.74–35.29; p = 0.007). Conclusion: ETDQ-7 is a useful outpatient triage tool for identifying patients with CRS who need objective audiological evaluation; it should not replace confirmatory testing.

title: Clinical Spectrum of Sexually Transmitted Infections and Treponemal Serological Profile Among Patients Living with HIV at a Tertiary Dermatovenereology Clinic in Surakarta, Indonesia: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study (2020–2026)
journal: Scientific Journal of Dermatology and Venereology
abstract: Background: Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection interact biologically, but data from Indonesian tertiary dermatovenereology clinics are scarce. Objective: To describe the clinical STI spectrum, coinfection multiplicity, and Venereal Disease Research Laboratory (VDRL) and Treponema pallidum hemagglutination assay (TPHA) results of HIV-positive patients at Dr. Moewardi Regional General Hospital, Surakarta, Indonesia (2020–2026). Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study analyzed medical records of 74 HIV-positive patients with STIs (ethics approval: 865/V/HREC/2026). Sociodemographics, STI diagnoses, multiplicity, and VDRL/TPHA results were summarized descriptively with Wilson 95% confidence intervals; agreement used Cohen's kappa (κ), and TPHA reactivity was explored by logistic regression. Results: Of 74 patients, 68 (91.89%) were male and 36 (48.65%) were aged 21–30 years (mean 29.70 years). Isolated condyloma acuminata predominated (n = 43, 58.11%), followed by isolated syphilis (n = 17, 22.97%), condyloma acuminata plus syphilis (n = 6, 8.11%), other polymicrobial STIs (n = 6, 8.11%), and molluscum contagiosum (n = 2, 2.70%). Single STIs occurred in 62 patients (83.78%) and multiple STIs in 12 (16.22%). VDRL was positive in 32 patients (43.24%; modal titer 1:16; maximum 1:512) and not done in 19 (25.68%). TPHA was reactive in 34 patients (45.95% overall; 61.82% of 55 tested; κ = 0.924); 11 of 51 patients with non-syphilitic STIs (21.57%) were TPHA-reactive without a syphilis diagnosis. Multiple STIs were associated with TPHA reactivity (aOR = 4.890, p = 0.0344). Conclusion: Condyloma acuminata and young adult male predominance characterized HIV-associated STIs here, and TPHA reactivity without a syphilis diagnosis supports considering paired VDRL/TPHA screening.

title: The Longitudinal Reflective Diary Model for Reflective Thinking Development and Future Leadership Readiness in Islamic Boarding Schools
abstract: Reflective diaries are widely used as learning and evaluation tools, yet their potential as longitudinal records of students’ reflective development remains underexplored in pesantren education. This study aims to examine the implementation of a longitudinal reflective diary programme, identify patterns of students’ reflective development, and analyse its pedagogical characteristics in relation to Problem-Based Learning (PBL). Employing a qualitative case study design, the research involved 20 second-year students of Kulliyatul Mu’allimin Al-Islamiyah (KMI) and analysed 80 diary entries collected between October 2025 and February 2026, supported by observations and programme documentation. Data were analysed using the interactive model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña through iterative coding and comparison across programme periods. The findings identified four interrelated and overlapping patterns of reflective development: adaptive reflection, social reflection, prospective reflection, and integrative reflection. These patterns indicate a gradual expansion from responses to immediate challenges towards social awareness, future-oriented planning, and the integration of personal, academic, spiritual, and social experiences. The diary programme also demonstrated several PBL-related characteristics, particularly authentic problem orientation, self-inquiry, reflection, and solution formulation, although it did not constitute a complete PBL implementation. The study contributes a conceptual model of reflective development and positions longitudinal reflective diaries as developmental archives with potential applications for future reflection and leadership learning. However, their contribution to actual leadership readiness requires further longitudinal investigation.

Do Tourist Levies Shorten Stays and Divert Visitors? A Quantitative Survey of Levy Design in India
journal: American Journal of Tourism and Hospitality
abstract: Visitor levies are spreading across Indian destinations, but the measures adopted so far differ in how the charge is structured (per night versus once per stay), how it is presented (included in the quoted price versus added at check-out) and whether the use of revenue is specified. This study tests, with primary survey data, whether these design features shape the behavioural margins a levy is meant to move: length of stay, off-site spending and diversion to untaxed alternatives. We administered a structured questionnaire to 150 overnight visitors across four Indian levy jurisdictions (Sikkim, Himachal Pradesh, Goa and Rajasthan) between July 2025 and March 2026. Respondents encountering a per-night levy reported significantly shorter actual stays than those encountering a flat, one-time levy (b = −0.61 nights, p < .001), and stays were shorter again when the levy was itemized at check-out rather than included in the booking price, an effect that operated largely through tax salience and pain-of-paying perceptions (both r > .37, p < .001). Destinations that communicated a specified use for levy revenue retained longer stays and higher off-site spending (both p < .001). Pain of paying, not salience alone, predicted the intention to substitute toward an untaxed neighbouring destination (odds ratio = 2.85, p = .004). A two-way analysis of variance confirmed additive, non-interacting effects of structure and presentation on length of stay, F(1, 146) = 13.6 and F (1, 131) = 13.1, respectively, both p < .001. A supplementary factor-analytic and cluster-analytic exploration in R recovered a clean three-factor structure underlying the perception scales and identified three visitor segments: skeptical low-trust visitors, price-sensitive avoiders, and unfazed high-spenders, which differ sharply in length of stay (2.96 to 4.75 nights) and displacement risk (13.3% to 52.0%). The findings support a mental-accounting and pain-of-paying account of levy design over a pure salience account, and they indicate that earmarking communication is a low-cost lever for destination managers to soften behavioural contraction. Implications for the design of tourist levies in India and directions for quasi-experimental follow-up work are discussed.

title: ENHANCED RECOVERY AFTER ELECTIVE CESAREAN SECTION (ERAS): A REVIEW OF CURRENT EVIDENCE AND DESIGN OF A PROSPECTIVE CONTROLLED STUDY
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Resume. Cesarean section (CS) accounted for 21.1% of births worldwide in 2010–2018, and the rate is projected to reach 28.5% by 2030. The Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) concept, first applied in colorectal surgery, has been adapted for CS by the ERAS Society, whose recommendations were updated in 2025. We reviewed the ERAS Society guidelines and two meta-analyses comparing ERAS with conventional care. In 10 studies with 16,391 patients, ERAS shortened hospital stay by 7.47 hours, halved the rate of postoperative complications (RR 0.50) and reduced pain scores, opioid use and hospital costs, with no change in readmissions. In 12 studies with 17,607 patients, ERAS reduced the time to first mobilization by 11.05 hours, the time to urinary catheter removal by 13.19 hours and opioid consumption by 21.85 mg morphine equivalents. The certainty of this evidence was rated low or very low, which justifies local controlled studies. We describe the design of a prospective controlled comparative study of 106 women aged 18–35 years undergoing elective CS at term: 30 managed according to an adapted ERAS protocol and 76 receiving traditional postoperative care. The outcomes include pain on the Visual Analogue Scale, opioid requirement, recovery of bowel function, mobilization, complications, length of stay, breastfeeding, psycho-emotional status, patient satisfaction and treatment costs. Keywords: cesarean section; enhanced recovery after surgery; ERAS; multimodal analgesia; early mobilization; length of hospital stay; breastfeeding.

Chyle Leak Conservative and Medical Management: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Outcomes Following Iatrogenic Injury
abstract: Background/Objectives: Iatrogenic chyle leaks after oncological surgery cause significant morbidity and mortality across specialties, yet management lacks consensus. This is the first cross-specialty systematic review and meta-analysis of conservative management for iatrogenic chyle leak using individual patient-level data. Methods: Following PRISMA guidelines, PubMed was searched to October 2026 for studies of adults with iatrogenic post-operative chyle leak managed conservatively. Primary outcomes were the requirement for surgery or interventional radiology, morbidity, and mortality. Secondary outcomes were length of stay, time to resolution, and fistula output. Exposed and unexposed patients were compared using Fisher’s exact and Mann-Whitney U tests, with Bonferroni correction (p < 0.00082). Pooled meta-analysis of primary outcomes was completed, with sensitivity analyses. Results: Eighteen studies (343 patients) were included after head and neck (40.5%), thoracic (33.5%), and abdominal (25.9%) operations. The pooled proportion requiring surgery was 20.9% (95% CI 12.5–32.7%), and chyle leak-related mortality was 6.2% (95% CI 2.4–15.3%). After Bonferroni correction, somatostatin analogues were associated with lower all-cause mortality and morbidity, shorter length of stay and time to resolution; suction drainage with favorable outcomes; and passive drainage with poorer outcomes. Within specialties, 7 of the 17 Bonferroni-significant associations persisted, two were reversed, three did not persist, and five could not be tested. Conclusions: The majority of patients were managed without surgery. Associations with favorable outcomes were likely influenced by specialty, index operation, and confounding treatments. Somatostatin analogues showed the most consistent association with favorable outcomes. Standardized diagnostic criteria, consistent reporting, and multicenter cross-specialty studies are required for an evidence-based, stepwise management pathway.

title: Effect of Multimodal Prehabilitation Versus No Prehabilitation in Patients Undergoing Colorectal Cancer Resections: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the effects of multimodal prehabilitation on perioperative outcomes in patients undergoing colorectal cancer resection. Methods Standard medical databases such as MEDLINE, Embase, PubMed, and CINAHL were searched to find randomised, controlled trials comparing multimodal prehabilitation versus no prehabilitation before colorectal cancer resections. All data were analysed using Review Manager Software 5.4, and the meta-analysis was performed with the random effect model analysis. Results A total of 10 studies were included recruiting 1101 patients undergoing either laparoscopic or open colorectal cancer resections. In the random effect model analysis, multimodal prehabilitation was associated with improved preoperative 6-minute walking distance (6-MWD) (Standardised mean difference [SMD]: 0.76; 95% CI [0.28, 1.23], z = 3.10, P = 0.002), and a smaller effect of borderline significance in postoperative 6-MWD (SMD: 0.42; 95% CI [0.00, 0.83], z = 1.97, P = 0.05). There was no significant difference in postoperative complications (Odds ratio [OR]: 0.76; 95% confidence interval [CI] [0.56, 1.04], z = 1.69, P = 0.09) or mortality risk (OR: 0.39; 95% CI [0.07, 2.07], z = 1.10, P = 0.27). In addition, there was no statistical significance in postoperative readmission rate (OR: 1.08; 95% CI [0.48, 2.42], z = 0.19, P = 0.85) or length of stay (MD: -0.10; 95% CI [-0.30, 0.10], z = 1.00, P = 0.32). Conclusion Multimodal prehabilitation improved preoperative functional capacity, with a smaller effect of borderline significance postoperatively; both estimates were subject to substantial heterogeneity. These improvements did not translate into statistically significant reductions in postoperative complications, mortality, readmission or length of stay. Adequately powered multicentre randomised trials using standardised protocols are required to determine whether improvements in functional capacity lead to clinically meaningful benefits.

ENHANCING HOTEL MANAGEMENT EFFICIENCY IN UZBEKISTAN UNDER THE CONDITIONS OF DIGITAL TOURISM PLATFORMS
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: The rapid diffusion of digital tourism platforms has reconfigured the way hotels attract demand, set prices and interact with guests, turning digital capability into a core determinant of managerial performance. This paper examines how hotel enterprises in Uzbekistan can convert the opportunities created by online travel agencies, metasearch engines and property management technologies into measurable efficiency gains. Drawing on official tourism statistics, a review of the national regulatory framework and a structured analysis of hotel performance indicators, the study identifies the principal structural constraints of the sector: pronounced seasonality, a short average length of stay, a growing dependence on commission-based intermediaries and the absence of internationally comparable metrics such as ADR, RevPAR and GOPPAR in national reporting. Building on these findings, the paper proposes an integrated framework for data-driven hotel management that links channel optimisation, revenue management and online reputation management into a single decision-making cycle. The results contribute to the hospitality management literature on emerging tourism destinations and offer practical guidance for hotel managers and policymakers.

title: Intravenous iron during established bacterial infection in hospitalized adults: a systematic review of clinical outcomes and comparative evidence
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This systematic review asks what clinical and hematologic outcomes are associated with therapeutic intravenous iron administered during established acute bacterial infection in hospitalized adults, compared with no intravenous iron during the same episode. Direct evidence requires actual administration during ongoing infection and separable outcomes. The review will assess infection progression or treatment failure, all-cause mortality, transfusion, hemoglobin response and length of stay. Comparator strategies, care settings and potentially overlapping cohorts will be handled separately where appropriate. This record describes the working review plan as of 24 November 2026. Searching, preliminary screening and full-text retrieval have begun. Feasibility work includes provisional source-linked outcome entries, whose use for formal extraction remains under review. The PROSPERO draft was saved on 18 November 2026 and remained unsubmitted when last checked. Formal duplicate extraction, appraisal and final synthesis are pending. Ibrahim A. AlMulla performed the preliminary title and abstract screening. The review uses his screening decisions and approvals. The deposit contains the working protocol dated 24 November 2026.

title: Clinical and perioperative outcomes of biportal endoscopic versus open/microscopic lumbar discectomy: a systematic review and meta-analysis
journal: The Egyptian Journal of Neurosurgery : the official publication of the Egyptian Society of Neurological Surgeons/Egyptian journal of neurosurgery
abstract: Background Lumbar disc herniation (LDH) is a common cause of back pain and disability, often requiring surgical intervention when conservative treatments fail. Open microdiscectomy (MD) has been the standard approach; however, minimally invasive unilateral biportal endoscopic discectomy (BED) is gaining popularity. Methods PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane databases were systematically searched from inception to August 2025. Only three studies (two randomised controlled trials and one retrospective comparative study) met the inclusion criteria, representing a major limitation of this meta-analysis. Outcomes included change in VAS leg pain, VAS back pain, Oswestry Disability Index (ODI), operation time, length of hospital stay, and complications. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed using Review Manager 5.4.1. Results No statistically significant difference was found between BED and MD for leg pain (MD 0.12; 95% CI − 0.31 to 0.55; P = 0.59) or back pain (MD − 0.04; 95% CI − 0.36 to 0.28; P = 0.81) at one year. Functional improvement (ODI) was also similar. Operative time and hospital stay did not differ significantly, though heterogeneity was high. The complication rate was statistically significant in the BED group (RR 1.46; 95% CI 1.06–2.01; P = 0.02). Sensitivity analysis excluding the observational study did not alter the primary outcome conclusions. Conclusion Unilateral biportal endoscopic discectomy offers similar pain and functional outcomes to microdiscectomy at one year but may be associated with a higher complication rate, likely reflecting the learning curve. The small number of included studies (n = 3) limits the strength of these conclusions. Unilateral biportal endoscopic discectomy offers similar pain and functional outcomes to microdiscectomy at one year but may be associated with a higher complication rate. However, attributing this finding to the learning curve remains speculative, as surgeon experience was not consistently reported across the included studies. Also, the small number of included studies (n = 3) limits the strength of these conclusions.

title: Silo-based delayed closure and sutureless closure compared with fascial closure in neonates with gastroschisis: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: Systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative studies in neonates with gastroschisis (fascial closure, delayed closure after a silo, and sutureless closure). Registered after data collection and analysis, as a post hoc registration of the completed review. The protocol was first registered in PROSPERO as CRD420261519114 and amended to describe the pairwise design, the complexity strata and the updated search. Question: how do delayed silo-based closure (DC) and sutureless closure (SL) compare with fascial closure (FC) on length of stay, ventilator days, parenteral nutrition, time to full enteral feeds, sepsis, necrotizing enterocolitis, mortality and umbilical hernia? Searches (22 November 2026): PubMed, Scopus, Cochrane Library, EBSCOhost MEDLINE with Full Text, Europe PMC, ClinicalTrials.gov and ten hand-searched journals. 42 studies were included, 35 with arm-level data (about 5,800 infants) and 7 in a narrative synthesis. Methods: pairwise random-effects meta-analysis (REML, Hartung-Knapp intervals, prediction intervals) with network and multilevel models as checks; ROBINS-I and RoB 2; GRADE. Data, code and search materials: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24486543, https://github.com/sharing-123/gastroschisis-closure-sr-ma and https://sharing-123.github.io/gastroschisis-closure-sr-ma/

title: Hospital diagnosis related group payment and inpatient efficiency expenditure and patient safety
abstract: Background: Diagnosis-related group (DRG) payment changes hospitals' financial incentives by linking reimbursement to case mix rather than individual services. Improvements in inpatient efficiency may coexist with changes in expenditure composition, patient selection and post-discharge care. We examined these outcomes together to assess the implications of hospital payment reform. Methods: We reviewed nonrandomized evaluations of hospital DRG and related case-based payment reforms. Outcomes were organized into inpatient efficiency, expenditure and patient financial burden, and quality and safety. Differences in payment arrangements, study designs, outcome definitions and effect scales constrain the comparability of the available estimates. Results: The evidence described changes in length of stay, total and component expenditure, readmission, mortality and hospital service patterns. Shorter hospital stays were reported in several settings, whereas expenditure and safety findings varied by population, payment arrangement and outcome definition. Changes in drug and consumable expenditure were not consistently accompanied by reductions in other spending categories. Interpretation was limited by differences in study design, follow-up and the effects being estimated. Conclusions: DRG payment may be associated with shorter inpatient stays, but shorter stays alone do not establish better care or lower health-system expenditure. Evaluation should jointly consider risk-adjusted safety, patient financial burden and the distribution of care across hospitals and settings. The magnitude and certainty of any pooled association require a synthesis restricted to comparable, independently verified estimates.

title: Characteristics of eligible patients with a hip fracture for the IronHip trial: Protocol and Statistical Analysis Plan for a cross-sectional study of enrolled and declining patients The nIronHip study
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: SUMMARYThe non-IronHip (nIronHip) study is a cross-sectional study including patients declining participation in the IronHip randomised controlled trial, which investigates the effect of intravenous iron on postoperative mobility in older patients with hip fracture (HF). HFs are increasing worldwide and are associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs. Thus, improving treatments are warranted. Most solid evidence comes from RCTs, but they may have low external validity among patients with HF, where impaired cognitive function and fatigue frequently reduce the inclusion rate based on informed consent. Hence, it is important to know the generalizability of an RCTs to the broader patient population.The primary aim of the nIronHip study is to assess the external validity of the IronHip trial by comparing eligible patients who agree to participate in the trial with eligible patients who declined participation in the IronHip trial but consent to the nIronHip study. The study will compare pre-fracture mobility, measured by the New Mobility Score (NMS). Secondarily, it will compare demographic and clinical characteristics (age, sex, frailty, comorbidity, anticoagulant use, fracture type, type of surgery, time to surgery, length of stay and postoperative haemoglobin), and document reasons for declining trial participation.The study is conducted across three Danish hospitals and includes patients aged 65 years or older who meet the eligibility criteria for the IronHip trial. By identifying potential differences between the trial population and the eligible population, the goal of the study is to evaluate the representativeness of the trial. The findings will contribute to understanding whether results from hip fracture trials can be generalized to the eligible population of patients with a HF.

title: Internações, óbitos hospitalares, permanência e valores pagos por infarto agudo do miocárdio no SUS, Brasil, 2015–2024: dados do SIH/SUS
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Dados agregados e públicos do Sistema de Informações Hospitalares do SUS (SIH/SUS) sobre internações com diagnóstico principal de infarto agudo do miocárdio (Lista de Morbidade CID-10), extraídos da plataforma TabNet do DATASUS, por ano de processamento (janeiro de 2015 a dezembro de 2024), sexo, faixa etária e região de residência. Variáveis: internações, óbitos hospitalares, dias de permanência e valor total pago pelo SUS (reais correntes), com mortalidade hospitalar, média de permanência e valor médio por internação calculados. Arquivos: iam_sus_2015_2024.csv (tabela organizada em formato longo); dados_brutos_tabnet.zip (13 exportações originais do TabNet); LEIAME.md (fonte, parâmetros de extração, dicionário de variáveis e observações para reanálise). Fonte: SIH/SUS – Morbidade Hospitalar do SUS por local de residência, TabNet/DATASUS (http://tabnet.datasus.gov.br/cgi/deftohtm.exe?sih/cnv/nruf.def). Extração em novembro de 2026. Valores monetários não corrigidos pela inflação. Dados agregados, sem identificação de pessoas. English: Aggregated public data from the Brazilian Hospital Information System (SIH/SUS, DATASUS TabNet) on hospitalizations with a principal diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction, by year of processing (2015–2024), sex, age group and region of residence: hospitalizations, in-hospital deaths, length of stay and total amount paid (nominal BRL). Includes a tidy long-format table, the original TabNet exports and a README.

title: PERSONALIZED MANAGEMENT OF SEPTIC SHOCK: ADVANCES, CONTROVERSIES, AND KNOWLEDGE GAPS FOLLOWING ANDROMEDA-SHOCK-2, TIGRIS, AND THE 2026 SURVIVING SEPSIS CAMPAIGN GUIDELINES
abstract: Septic shock is a critical condition characterized by circulatory, cellular, and metabolic abnormalities associated with high morbidity and mortality. The heterogeneity of its pathophysiological mechanisms limits the effectiveness of uniform strategies and has encouraged individualized approaches. This narrative review critically analyzes the advances, controversies, and knowledge gaps in personalized management of septic shock in light of three recent publications: the ANDROMEDA-SHOCK-2 trial, the Tigris trial, and the 2026 Surviving Sepsis Campaign (SSC) guidelines, complemented by pathophysiological studies and earlier trials on resuscitation, vasopressor targets, and phenotypes. In ANDROMEDA-SHOCK-2, which included 1,467 patients with early septic shock, a personalized resuscitation strategy targeting capillary refill time was superior to usual care for a hierarchical composite of mortality, duration of vital support, and hospital length of stay (win ratio 1.16), mainly through shorter vital support, without a demonstrated isolated reduction in mortality. Tigris, a Bayesian open-label trial in 157 patients with endotoxic septic shock and high endotoxin activity, found posterior probabilities of benefit of 95.3% for 28-day mortality and 99.4% for 90-day mortality with polymyxin B hemoadsorption, but its small size, open design, and use of prior information limit generalization. The SSC 2026 guidelines endorse dynamic measures of fluid responsiveness and capillary refill time as adjuncts, maintain an initial mean arterial pressure target of 65 mmHg, and suggest against polymyxin B hemoperfusion, as Tigris was published after the guideline. Personalized management is promising, but it should preserve core interventions, weigh the certainty of evidence, and avoid extrapolating results from selected populations.

title: Impact of race on surgical risk and outcomes of head and neck free-flap reconstruction: a national database analysis of 5,206 reconstructions
abstract: Background Surgical free flaps are often used for head and neck (H&N) reconstruction for defects from cancer, trauma, and congenital anomalies. While socioeconomic variables have been studied in the H&N cancer population, racial disparities in H&N free-flap reconstruethicction need to be further studied. This study examines differences in comorbidities and outcomes between White and non-White patients undergoing H&N free-flap reconstruction. Methods Using the National Surgical Quality Improvement Program Database, patients undergoing H&N reconstructions were classified into White and non-White racial groups. Statistical associations were assessed using univariate chi-square and multivariate regression analyses in SPSS. Results Of 5,026 patients, 4,111(82%) were White and 915(18%) were non-White. Non-White patients were younger(p < 0.001), had longer lengths of stay(p = 0.001), and had longer operative times(p < 0.001). There was a higher incidence of diabetes mellitus(p = 0.005) and infected wounds(p = 0.010) in the non-White group. In comparison, White patients had a higher incidence of preoperative wound infection(p = 0.002) and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease(p = 0.01). Non-White patients were 1.65 times more likely to experience bleeding(p < 0.001), 2.08 times more likely to undergo flap failure(p < 0.05), and 1.65 times more likely to experience surgical complications(p < 0.001) after adjusting for pre-operative characteristics. Conclusions This study emphasizes racial disparities for free-flap reconstruction in the H&N population, suggesting an association between socioeconomic determinants and increased risk of flap failure in non-White patients. Increased awareness of racial disparities in H&N free-flap reconstruction amongst surgeons can help improve treatment for those respective populations. Level of Evidence III

title: Tazkiyah dan Pembentukan Karakter dalam QS. Al-Baqarah 151: Perspektif Pendidikan Pesantren
abstract: This study aims to analyze the concept of tazkiyah in QS. Al-Baqarah [2]:151 as a foundation for the formation of human morality and character, as well as to contextualize it within the educational traditions of Islamic boarding schools (pesantren). The study is motivated by the importance of character education that is not merely oriented toward the transfer of moral knowledge but also emphasizes the internalization of spiritual values and the transformation of students' behavior. This research employs a qualitative approach using library research through an integrative literature review. Data were collected through documentation of the Qur'anic text, Qur'anic exegesis literature, scholarly journal articles, and various studies relevant to the concepts of tazkiyah, character education, and pesantren education. Data analysis was conducted using interpretive thematic analysis and document analysis to identify the relationship between Qur'anic values and the mechanisms of character formation. The findings indicate that tazkiyah in QS. Al-Baqarah [2]:151 plays a significant role in moral education through the integration of three functions of Prophetic education: tilāwah al-āyāt, tazkiyah, and ta‘līm al-kitāb wa al-ḥikmah. These three functions constitute a conceptual unity that integrates the spiritual, moral, and intellectual dimensions of education. In the context of pesantren, the values of tazkiyah can be implemented through the exemplary conduct of kiai and educators, the habituation of positive behaviors, spiritual development, religious instruction, and institutional culture. This study proposes a conceptual framework for tazkiyah-based character education that connects the internalization of divine revelation, moral purification, and the enhancement of knowledge and wisdom. Therefore, tazkiyah can serve as a moral-spiritual principle for developing integrative character education within the pesantren environment.

title: Outcomes of Semiconstrained and Nonconstrained Implants in Patients Undergoing Cervical Disk Arthroplasty
Probiotics in Enteral Nutrition for the Management of Gastrointestinal Symptoms: A Systematic Review of Randomised Controlled Trials
abstract: Enteral nutrition (EN) is the preferred route of nutritional support for patients with a functional gastrointestinal tract who cannot meet their requirements orally. Despite its benefits, EN is frequently complicated by gastrointestinal symptoms that impair nutritional delivery. Probiotics and synbiotics have been proposed as adjunctive strategies, but evidence remains heterogeneous. This review was reported with reference to the 2020 Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidance. PubMed, including MEDLINE-indexed records, was searched for English-language randomised controlled trials (RCTs) published from 1 January 2010 through 5 November 2026. Adults aged ≥18 years receiving EN were eligible. Probiotic or synbiotic interventions were compared with placebo, EN without probiotics, fibre-enriched EN, or an active prophylactic antibiotic, depending on the trial. Risk of bias was assessed using the revised Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomised trials, and certainty of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation framework. Narrative synthesis was used because substantial heterogeneity in populations, interventions, comparators, and outcome definitions precluded meaningful pooling; clinically coherent subgroup meta-analyses were considered but were not feasible because each subgroup contained too few comparable studies. Nine RCTs involving 475 participants in eligible comparisons were included; mean ages across intervention groups were approximately 41-68 years. Four trials reported statistically significant between-group reductions in diarrhoea outcomes, while one additional trial reported a significant reduction only in liquid-stool frequency. One additional trial reported within-group improvement in both arms without demonstrating a between-group treatment effect. Effects on vomiting, abdominal pain, flatulence, albumin, mortality, length of stay, and body mass index were inconsistent or sparsely reported. Three studies had high risk of bias, two raised some concerns, and four had low risk. Certainty of evidence was low to very low across outcomes. Probiotics or synbiotics may benefit selected EN populations, particularly in specific oncology, radiation-enteritis, and postoperative settings. Still, statistically significant between-group superiority was demonstrated in fewer than half of the small, heterogeneous trials. The evidence does not support universal supplementation, and adequately powered, strain-specific RCTs with harmonised outcomes are required.

title: Safety and efficacy of Esketamine - Dexmedetomidine combination versus Dexmedetomidine monotherapy for hyperactive delirium in ICU patients on non-Invasive respiratory support (SEED-NIRS trial): study protocol of a randomized controlled trial
abstract: Background Approximately 36% of ICU patients receiving non-invasive respiratory support develop hyperactive delirium. These conditions are major drivers of support intolerance and failure, with current failure rates for non-invasive support ranging from 15% to 38%. Escalating conventional sedation often carries the risk of respiratory depression, potentially necessitating iatrogenic intubation. Dexmedetomidine is recommended to prevent delirium but has a high incidence of bradycardia, hypotension and a high failure rate, whereas esketamine provides rapid sedation and analgesia with minimal respiratory depression but may cause sympathetic and psychotomimetic adverse effects. Given their distinct pharmacological profiles and effects on different neurobiological pathways implicated in delirium, it is hypothesized that the combination may exert complementary pharmacological effects; however, this hypothesis requires validation in well-designed clinical trials. Methods This SEED-NIRS trial is an investigator-initiated, randomized, controlled, single-blind, superiority trial conducted in a tertiary teaching hospital in China. Participants with hyperactive delirium receiving non-invasive respiratory support will be randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either esketamine combined with dexmedetomidine (Es-Dex) or dexmedetomidine monotherapy (Dex). The primary outcome is a hierarchical composite endpoint within 7 days, analyzed via the win ratio (WR) approach, prioritizing (in order): (1) requirement for endotracheal intubation, (2) duration of delirium, and (3) duration of agitation. Secondary outcomes include ventilator-free and/or delirium-free days, delirium recurrence, rescue antipsychotic medications in the first 7 days, Critical-Care Pain Observation Tool (CPOT)/Numeric Rating Scale - Visually enlarged (NRS-V) scores, Athens Insomnia Scale (AIS) scores, the length of ICU stay, all-cause mortality at day 28, the incidence of adverse events. Discussion This SEED-NIRS trial addresses a critical clinical dilemma in non-invasive ICU patients: achieving optimal sedation for agitated patients while avoiding the increasing risk of endotracheal intubation for respiratory depression. By employing a WR approach, this study reflects the clinical priority of intubation avoidance while accounting for the burden of delirium. The results are expected to provide high-quality evidence for a novel, hemodynamically stable, and respiratory-sparing sedation strategy in the ICU patients on non-invasive respiratory support. Clinical Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov, identifier NCT07377981.

title: Fiscal, labour market and distributive effects of alternative free senior high school financing reforms in Ghana: a linked microsimulation and dynamic CGE analysis
abstract: This study combines the GHAMOD microsimulation model, which is from the pool of SOUTHMOD models by UNU-WIDER, and IFPRI’s RIAPA dynamic CGE model to investigate the fiscal and economy-wide impacts of educational reforms in Ghana’s Free Senior High School (FSHS) policy. Introduced in 2017/2018, the FSHS policy aims to improve access to secondary education, particularly for the poor. However, like several other subsidy interventions in developing countries, the policy has introduced significant fiscal and implementation challenges as well including overstretched facilities, impaired subsidy payment by the government for feeding, teaching and learning materials. Thus, putting a strain on quality of education. The paper simulates the current universal FSHS policy and six alternative reforms that explore efficiency, fiscal sustainability, and social equity. Specifically, we evaluate policy effectiveness and distributive effects of the status quo ‘universal FSHS grant’ with targeted scenarios with respect to (1) a beneficiary’s boarding/residency status (2) poverty status of beneficiary students (means-tested), and (3) capped benefit for all beneficiaries. These scenarios are evaluated on long term impacts on government savings, poverty, inequality, sectoral growth, and labour market outcomes up to 2040. Our findings indicate that targeted reforms do not only lead to increased fiscal savings, which when reinvested offsets non-market incomes of households from the limited grant transfer by stimulating sectorial growth, employment and positive distributive impact on households. We are able to demonstrate that simpler and less-costly non-means-tested schemes based on residency or capped benefits could be deployed to mitigate the fiscal constraints posed by the current form of the policy while yielding significant positive fiscal and distributive impacts. The findings from the study contribute to deepening the FSHS policy discourse in Ghana. Specifically, the simulated reforms could guide the pursuit toward a targeted FSHS policy which is fair and fiscally sustainable.

title: Robot-assisted kinematic versus mechanical alignment in total knee arthroplasty: a comparative clinical study
abstract: Personalised alignment techniques have gained significant attention to improve patient satisfaction after total knee arthroplasty (TKA). This study aims to compare the functional outcomes of patients undergoing knee replacement surgery with kinematic alignment (KA) versus those with mechanical alignment (MA). This retrospective cohort study analyzed patients who underwent robotic-assisted unilateral total knee arthroplasty between December 2023 and March 2024. Based on the intraoperative alignment technique, patients were assigned to either a KA group or a MA group. Using 1:1 propensity score matching on age, sex, BMI, and Kellgren–Lawrence grade, 30 patients were assigned to each group, resulting in a total of 60 patients included for analysis. Postoperative functional outcomes were analysed at different time points. After propensity score matching, 30 patients were included in each group (total n = 60); because all patients were successfully matched, the matched cohort was identical to the original cohort. Baseline characteristics did not differ significantly between the two groups (all P > 0.05), although residual imbalance remained for BMI (standardised mean difference [SMD] 0.43) and sex (SMD 0.34). Compared with the MA group, the KA group had significantly longer operative time (75.33 ± 15.53 vs. 66.47 ± 16.67 min, P = 0.037), less intraoperative blood loss (207.67 ± 29.88 vs. 231.17 ± 33.73 mL, P = 0.006), and shorter total length of stay from admission to discharge (3.97 ± 0.85 vs. 4.87 ± 1.07 d, P = 0.001). At 1, 3, and 6 months postoperatively, the KA group showed significantly lower VAS scores, higher Oxford Knee Score (OKS), and better Forgotten Joint Score (FJS) and WOMAC scores ( P < 0.05). At 1 year postoperatively, the KA group continued to demonstrate superior OKS, FJS, WOMAC, and KSS symptom, satisfaction and expectation subscales compared with MA ( P < 0.05). However, at 2 years, most outcome differences were no longer statistically significant except for FJS ( P = 0.031). General health measured with the VR-12 was higher in the MA group than in the KA group at 1 month ( P < 0.001). No major perioperative or postoperative complications occurred in either group. Compared to MA, KA may lead to better early postoperative outcomes in satisfaction, function, and joint awareness. These findings should be interpreted with caution because of the retrospective design, the residual baseline imbalance remaining after matching, and the absence of postoperative alignment data. Larger long-term studies are needed to confirm its sustained efficacy. The study has been registered on the International Traditional Medicine Clinical Trial registry platform and has been assigned a unique identifying number (ITMCTR2025002049). Registration date: 2025-10-28, retrospectively registered.

title: Perfil clínico e epidemiológico de crianças com malária no Hospital Municipal de Menongue em Angola
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: RESUMO Este estudo analisa o perfil clínico e epidemiológico da malária em crianças internadas no Hospital Municipal de Menongue, unidade hospitalar de nível primário localizada na província do Cuando Cubango, Angola. O objetivo do estudo foi analisar as características clínicas e epidemiológicas das crianças internadas com diagnóstico de malária durante o ano de 2021. Trata-se de um estudo descritivo, retrospectivo e de abordagem quantitativa, baseado na análise de registros hospitalares. A amostra foi constituída por 300 pacientes pediátricos internados com diagnóstico confirmado de malária. As variáveis analisadas incluíram idade, sexo, proveniência, sinais e sintomas, complicações, sazonalidade dos casos, tratamento administrado, tempo de internamento e desfecho clínico. Os resultados demonstraram que crianças menores de cinco anos representaram a maioria dos casos de internamento, correspondendo a 63% da amostra. Observou-se também predominância de pacientes provenientes de bairros periféricos da cidade de Menongue. Entre as manifestações clínicas mais frequentes destacaram-se febre, diarreia e vómitos. A principal complicação identificada foi a anemia. Em relação ao desfecho clínico, a maioria dos pacientes evoluiu para alta hospitalar, enquanto uma menor proporção resultou em transferências, fugas e óbitos. Os resultados evidenciam que a malária continua sendo um importante problema de saúde pública em Angola, particularmente entre crianças, reforçando a necessidade de fortalecer estratégias de prevenção, diagnóstico precoce e tratamento adequado. Palavras-chave: Malária. Perfil Clínico. Epidemiologia. Crianças. ABSTRACT This study analyzes the clinical and epidemiological profile of malaria in children admitted to the Municipal Hospital of Menongue, a primary-level hospital located in Cuando Cubango Province, Angola. The objective of the study was to analyze the clinical and epidemiological characteristics of children hospitalized with malaria during the year 2021. This is a descriptive, retrospective study with a quantitative approach, based on the analysis of hospital records. The sample consisted of 300 pediatric patients hospitalized with confirmed malaria diagnosis. The variables analyzed included age, sex, origin, clinical signs and symptoms, complications, seasonal distribution of cases, treatment administered, length of hospital stay and clinical outcomes. The results showed that children under five years of age accounted for the majority of hospitalizations. Most patients were from peripheral neighborhoods of Menongue. The most frequent clinical manifestations were fever, diarrhea and vomiting. The main complication identified was anemia. Regarding clinical outcomes, most patients were discharged from the hospital, while smaller proportions resulted in transfers, absconding and deaths. The findings indicate that malaria remains a major public health problem in Angola, especially among children, highlighting the importance of strengthening prevention strategies, early diagnosis and adequate treatment. Keywords: Malaria. Clinical Profile. Epidemiology. Children.

title: Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangiopancreatography Versus Surgical Biliary Diversion for the Treatment of Complex Choledocholithiasis
abstract: Introduction and Aims: Complex choledocholithiasis (CC) affects approximately 15% of patients with choledocholithiasis. Treatment depends on available resources and specialist preferences. This study compared immediate outcomes of endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) versus surgical biliodigestive derivation (SBDD) for CC treatment. Methods: This retrospective study analyzed records of patients treated for CC — defined by common bile duct (CBD) diameter > 15 mm, stones > 15 mm, multiple stones, and/or intrahepatic stones — at a tertiary university hospital between 2004 and 2017, via ERCP or SBDD (conventional or laparoscopic). Results: 183 patients were divided into two groups: ERCP (n = 140, 76.5%) and SBDD (n = 43, 23.5%). Groups were comparable in age, gender, comorbidities, cholangitis, and cholestasis. SBDD patients had significantly longer symptom duration, larger CBD diameter, and larger stones. Adverse event rates were 6.4% (ERCP) vs. 25.6% (SBDD) (p < 0.005). In-hospital mortality was 1.4% vs. 2.3% (p > 0.05). Stone recurrence was 5% vs. 4.65% (p > 0.05). Therapeutic success reached 95% (ERCP) and 100% (SBDD) (p > 0.05). Younger patients with larger stones had higher ERCP failure likelihood. Among ERCP failures, bilirubin levels at diagnosis were significantly elevated (p < 0.05). Larger stones and higher bilirubin were also associated with requiring two or more ERCP sessions for CBD clearance. Conclusions: Both approaches were effective, with no difference in recurrence or mortality. SBDD achieved higher therapeutic success but with significantly greater morbidity and longer hospitalization. Elevated direct and total bilirubin and stones > 15 mm were associated with ERCP failure in achieving complete CBD clearance.

title: Selected Factors Affecting Turnover Intention of Finance Sector Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) Employees in Colombo District: Mediating Role of Organizational Commitment & Moderating Role of Alternative Job Opportunities
abstract: Employee Turnover Intention problem has become an emerging problem in most Sri Lankan contexts, and it can be majorly seen in the Finance Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) sector. Employee Turnover Intention is the employee’s tendency to leave the organizations due to distinct factors such as the imbalance between work and individual life. There were less studies concerned the Finance BPO service sector employees and therefore the main purpose of this study is to identify the factors affecting Employee Turnover Intention in Finance – BPO sector employees in Sri Lanka with the mediating effect of organizational commitment & the moderating variable of alternative job opportunities. Accordingly, the population of this study consists of all the employees who are working in Finance BPO sector in Sri Lankan context and the sample of this study consists of the employees of Finance BPO sector in top 10 commercialized BPO organizations in Sri Lanka. Guided by Herzberg's Two-Factor Theory, this study investigates four primary factors: rewards, career development opportunities, working environment & job satisfaction significantly influence employees’ turnover intention while the organizational commitment mediating the relationship between the factors affecting to the employee turnover intention and the employee turnover intention & alternative job opportunities moderating the relationship between the organizational commitment and the employee turnover intention The researcher has used the main data collection method of survey by distributing the questionnaire via online (Google Form) to the selected sample and succeeded in collecting 200 respondents. The researcher has used the SPSS Statistical Software to identify significant relationships. The results revealed that all the variables have significant negative impact on employees’ turnover intention. Furthermore, the organizational commitment mediates significantly the factors affecting the employees’ turnover intention & the alternative job opportunities moderates significantly in the relationship between the organizational commitment and the employees’ turnover intention. Overall, the findings confirm that the selected factors are significantly influencing the employees’ turnover intention, with career growth opportunities emerging as the most influential variable & working environment emerging as the least influential variable. The results offer valuable insights for BPO managers and HR practitioners in developing targeted retention strategies that enhance employee satisfaction and organizational stability.

title: Trajectories of physical and functional impairment in cancer survivors: Associations with emergency and urgent care utilization and cancer rehabilitation referrals
abstract: PURPOSE: This study examined physical function impairment (PFI) trajectories among outpatient cancer survivors in a large Midwestern academic health care system. The authors hypothesized that PFI would be common and vary across time depending on extent of disease and care phase. They evaluated associations between trajectories and rehabilitation services referral (RSR) and urgent unplanned health care utilization (HCU; emergency department, cancer center urgent care visits). METHODS: The authors sampled adults (n = 2254) who completed Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System-Physical Function (PROMIS-PF) surveys during the first 36 months after cancer diagnosis. PROMIS-PF T scores ≤40 represented PFI. They used group-based trajectory modeling to identify PFI trajectories and mixed effects regression comparing trajectories with RSR and HCU over time. RESULTS: The authors identified four PFI trajectories: (1) low probability but steady ("low steady," 64%); (2) decreasing probability ("decreasing," 13%); (3) increasing probability ("increasing," 9%); and (4) high probability that remained high ("high steady," 14%). Compared to trajectory 1, patients in trajectories 2-4 were significantly more likely to have HCU and receive RSRs, although group differences were mixed. RSRs declined rapidly for all four trajectories. DISCUSSION: A sizeable minority experienced PFI during the first 3 years after cancer diagnosis with nuanced differences for RSRs and HCU. Patients in trajectories 2, 3, and especially 4, may need to be targeted for early and continued monitoring for impairment and RSR. CONCLUSIONS: PROMIS-PF effectively identified variation across patients and time. Future research may explore whether RSRs based on PROMIS-PF screening are associated with effective cancer rehabilitation triaging and reduced HCU.

title: An integrated intervention of spinal cord stimulation and multidisciplinary rehabilitation for chronic neuropathic leg pain: a single-case experimental design protocol
abstract: Neuropathic pain is a debilitating condition affecting multiple dimensions of patients' lives, warranting multidisciplinary treatment from a biopsychosocial perspective. Spinal cord stimulation (SCS) is a well-established treatment that reduces pain intensity by implanting a generator that delivers electrical impulses to the spinal cord. Until now, SCS primarily has been studied as monotherapy, not within a biopsychosocial framework. This protocol describes a multidisciplinary intervention combining SCS with physical and psychological rehabilitation, evaluated using a single-case experimental design (SCED). In contrast to randomized controlled trials (RCTs), the main analysis level is within-participants, rather than at the group level, thus results cannot be generalized to a broader population. The study is a single-center, open-label trial employing a randomized-start-point AB design across 10 participants with chronic neuropathic pain in one or both legs, caused by either persistent spinal pain syndrome or focal peripheral nerve injury. The intervention bundle consists of SCS, standardized physiotherapy, and psychological treatment with Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT) delivered over 12 weeks. The design allows for individualization of SCS programming and rehabilitation components, and includes five phases: a 5-week pre-implantation baseline (A1), a randomized post-implantation baseline of 2,3 or 4 weeks with no stimulation (A2), a 12-week intervention period [split into two analytical phases of 6 weeks (B1 and B2)], and a 5-week follow-up 6 months after implantation. Primary outcomes are pain intensity in the leg(s) measured by numeric rating scale (0–10) and physical function measured by PROMIS-29, both assessed three times weekly in all phases. Effects will be analyzed using visual analysis, standardized mean differences, and baseline-corrected Tau. We expect an early reduction in pain intensity following SCS implantation, with gradual improvement in physical function emerging later as the rehabilitation components take effect. This protocol provides a reproducible framework for evaluating complex multidisciplinary interventions in chronic neuropathic pain and applies SCED methodology in a way that can contribute to new knowledge in the SCS field. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT07403331; registered February 2, 2026.

title: Surgical Management of Cervical Disc Herniation in a Resource-Limited Setting: Outcomes and Challenges
journal: Journal of Pak International Medical College
abstract: Objectives: To evaluate clinical and functional outcomes and identify perioperative and health-system challenges among patients undergoing surgical treatment for symptomatic cervical disc herniation in a resource-limited tertiary-care hospital. Methodology: This Retrospective Observational Study Was Conducted In The Department Of Neurosurgery, MMC/BKMC mardan, From January To December 2025. We included 100 consecutive adult patients with MRI-confirmed symptomatic cervical disc herniation who underwent surgical treatment. We retrospectively extracted demographic, clinical, radiological, operative, postoperative, and health-system data from medical records. We assessed pain and functional disability using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) and Neck Disability Index (NDI), respectively, before surgery and at 6-month follow-up. Results: Among 100 patients, 62% were male, and 38% were female, with a mean age of 47.8 ± 11.4 years. The most frequently affected level was C5–C6 (44%), followed by C6–C7 (31%). Radiculopathy was present in 71% of patients and myelopathy in 29%. We performed ACDF in 82% of patients, while 18% underwent discectomy without fusion. Mean VAS decreased from 7.6 ± 1.2 preoperatively to 2.3 ± 1.1 at 6 months, while mean NDI decreased from 34.5 ± 8.7 to 12.8 ± 5.4 (both p<0.001). Postoperative complications occurred in 11% of patients. Documented health-system barriers included delayed MRI access (27%), implant shortages (19%), and operating-room scheduling delays (22%). Conclusion: In this single-center retrospective cohort, surgical treatment of symptomatic cervical disc herniation was associated with substantial improvements in pain and functional disability at 6 months. Delays in MRI access, implant availability, and operating-room scheduling represented important health-system challenges

title: Neighborhood disadvantage and same-day surgical cancellation in children: a multispecialty cohort study
abstract: Purpose: Day-of-surgery cancellations (DoSCs) disrupt pediatric surgical care and may disproportionately affect socially disadvantaged groups. We examined associations between neighborhood social vulnerability and DoSC across pediatric surgical specialties. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed elective surgical encounters at a freestanding tertiary children’s hospital (2020–2025). Geocoded residential addresses were linked to 2020 CDC Social Vulnerability Index (SVI) data. Encounters were classified as completed, non-DoSC, or DoSC. Multivariable logistic regression with cluster-robust standard errors assessed associations of overall SVI and race with DoSC, adjusting for season and year. Documented cancellation reasons were compared across SVI terciles. Results: Among 72,489 encounters, 4,066 (5.6%) were DoSCs. Rates increased across SVI terciles from 4.0% to 9.2% (p < 0.001). Higher SVI (OR 2.20, 95% CI 1.94–2.49) and Black race (OR 1.89, 95% CI 1.74–2.07) were independently associated with DoSC; the race association persisted after excluding SVI’s race theme. Among DoSCs, the proportion attributed to no-shows increased with vulnerability (2.7%–14.1%), whereas clinical reasons declined. Associations remained stable across pandemic and post-pandemic eras. Conclusion: Neighborhood social vulnerability and Black race were independently associated with pediatric DoSC across specialties. These findings identify higher-risk encounters and support prospective evaluation of engagement-focused preoperative interventions.

title: Operational Efficiency, Queue-Time Reductions, and Cost-Effectiveness of AI-Driven Patient Intake Systems in US Ambulatory and Primary Care: A Systematic Review and Quantitative Evidence Synthesis
journal: Open Access Public Health and Health Administration Review
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-driven patient intake systems are increasingly deployed in ambulatory and primary care workflows to collect medical histories, identify clinical risks prior to consultation, and generate structured summaries for clinicians. Unlike ambient documentation scribes, these tools interact directly with patients before or at the start of clinical encounters. This systematic review synthesized empirical evidence on the operational efficiency, intake performance, queue-time outcomes, and cost-effectiveness of AI-driven patient intake systems in US ambulatory and primary care settings in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Comprehensive searches across 11 databases and registries through September 25, 2026, yielded 1,620 total records (1,608 database records and 12 via citation chaining). Following duplicate removal (n = 524) and title/abstract screening (n = 1,096), 40 full-text reports were assessed, resulting in 4 core empirical studies supported by contextual workflow evaluations that reported that 80.0% of participants believed conversational AI improved physician understanding of their health, while 102,059 virtual encounters were analyzed and found clinicians selected an AI-generated diagnosis in 84.2% of cases. Studies confirmed prospective ambulatory safety under human oversight. A study demonstrated 93.0% usability and 97.9% completion in outpatient care. Methodological quality appraisal indicated moderate risk of bias across small pilot cohorts and preliminary certainty for preprint evidence. Current evidence supports technical feasibility, patient acceptability, and diagnostic utility, but evidence for direct queue-time reductions or realized financial savings remains preliminary and heterogeneous. Future multi-center-controlled trials utilizing objective electronic health record (EHR) timestamps, formal health economic evaluations, and equity monitoring frameworks are required.

title: The Multi-Office Accelerator Team (MOAT) Seed Project
abstract: Particle accelerators are essential scientific infrastructure, but their design and operation remain constrained by machine complexity, fragmented facility knowledge, and the practical difficulty of deploying artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) methods beyond narrow, facility-specific applications. The Multi-Office Accelerator Team (MOAT) Seed project was launched under the U.S. Department of Energy Genesis Mission to develop shared AI/ML and agentic AI capabilities for accelerator science across the DOE complex. This paper presents early results from the MOAT Seed collaboration, with emphasis on the Osprey agentic AI platform. We describe how Osprey connects advanced reasoning models with accelerator control-system data, archives, electronic logbooks, simulation tools, and domain-specific workflows. Examples across multiple national laboratories demonstrate the use of Osprey and agentic AI more broadly for archived-data analysis, real-time troubleshooting, measurement and characterization, response-matrix analysis, control-loop generation, downtime analysis, and accelerator design. These initial demonstrations show that agentic workflows can substantially reduce the effort required to perform analyses and design studies that traditionally demand custom scripting and expert intervention, while also enabling shared capabilities to transfer across facilities. We also summarize related progress toward digital twins and virtual accelerators, and discuss how the MOAT approach can support broader deployment of reusable AI infrastructure for accelerator operations and design.

Implementing Screening Questionnaires and a Fish Bone Diagram-Based Program to Enhance the Ability of DBW Education in Hemodialysis Nurses
abstract: Background: Dry body weight evaluation to detect high and low hydration status is paramount in daily hemodialysis practice. Our aim is to implement screening questionnaires and fish bone diagram-based program to improve the ability of dry body weight education of hemodialysis nurses. Methods: This pioneer research by four staff members was initially authorized by the medical quality and patient safety talent training project and competition meeting initiated by the administrative units of Taipei City Hospital and then approved by Taipei City Hospital Research Ethics Committee with the case number of TCHIRB-11206015.The study began with screening questionnaires of educational test about dry body weight education. Subsequently, teams composed of nurse faculty were evaluated for three domains of dry body weight evaluation, such as hemodialysis nurse’s knowledge and education skills on dry body weight, body components and body weight assessment equipment and tools. A fish bone diagram for root cause analysis was implemented with improvement of knowledge and skills of dry body weight evaluation of nurse faculty, methods of dry body weight evaluation, equipment for dry body weight evaluation, tools of dry body weight evaluation, environment of dry body weight evaluation, and materials of dry body weight evaluation. Results: Wilcoxon Signed Ranks Test are used to identify statistically significant differences in the scores of between the domain 1 and domain 2, between domain 1 and domain 2A, and between domain 1 and domain 2B. The screening questionnaires revealed. A Fish bone diagram was completed and presented to improve the ability of dry body weight education of hemodialysis nurses with dry body evaluation education sheet, poster and ever scam education software. In addition, suggestions for improving the ability of dry body weight education include inclusion of nutritional staff involvement, post- dialysis cardiac echo for inferior vena diameter, chest ultrasound for B lines, Crit-Line for blood volume monitor, DEXA for body composition evaluation, and selection of topics of food salt and water content, techniques and environment of dry body weight evaluation, bio-impedance, and upper arm anthropometry. Conclusions: Accurate evaluation of dry body weight by clinical evaluation, equipment and tools not only can prevent hemodialysis patients from deterioration of cardiopulmonary function and the chance of emergency dialysis due to high hydration status but also prevent patients from hospitalization due to shock and thrombotic complications due to low hydration status, and therefore reduce their medical costs and improve patient satisfaction and trust in the hospital.

title: Awareness of triage systems and trauma management protocols among emergency unit staff in district hospitals in the Ashanti Region of Ghana: a cross-sectional study
abstract: To determine whether staff at district-level hospitals in the Ashanti Region of Ghana were aware of triage systems and trauma protocols being in place at their hospitals. We interviewed randomly-selected health workers (doctors, physician assistants, nurses) in emergency units of 15 purposively-selected district-level hospitals. Factors associated with awareness of triage systems and trauma protocols were assessed with multivariable logistic regression. 256 health workers were interviewed. Most reported that their hospital had a triage system (85.5%) and a trauma protocol (86.7%). Hospitals ranged from 0% to 43% of respondents being unaware of a triage system. Staff at faith-based hospitals were more likely to be aware of a triage system at their hospital than government hospital staff (aOR = 20.54; 95%CI 2.72–155.06; p = 0.003). Private hospital staff were less likely to be aware of a triage system (aOR = 0.35; 95%CI 0.13–0.98; p = 0.046). Faith-based hospital staff were more likely to be aware of a trauma protocol (aOR = 4.23; 95%CI 1.40–12.71, p = 0.010). Many staff were not aware that their hospitals had these tools in place, especially at government and private hospitals. Solutions include periodic training on triage and trauma protocols and having printed copies of these tools on display in emergency units.

title: Missed Nursing Care and Barriers to Care in a Burn Center: A Cross-Sectional Study
abstract: Purpose: This study aimed to determine the level of missed nursing care and identify barriers to nursing care among nurses working in a burn center.Methods: This descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted in November 2025 in the burn intensive care unit and burn ward of a city hospital in Istanbul, Türkiye. Data were collected from 26 nurses using a Sociodemographic Information Form and the Missed Nursing Care Questionnaire. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, appropriate groupcomparison tests, and Pearson correlation analysis.Results: The mean MNCQ Part A (Missed Nursing Care) score was 1.39±0.38, and the mean Part B (Reasons for Missed Nursing Care) score was 3.27±0.54. Part B scores were higher among male nurses than female nurses (3.60±0.04 vs. 3.22±0.47, p=0.001). Part A scores were higher among nurses working in the burn intensive care unit than among those working in the burn ward (1.53±0.30 vs. 1.23±0.42, p=0.045). Part B scores also differed according to intention to leave the institution (p=0.002). The most frequently perceived consequences of missed nursing care were prolonged hospital stay (73.1%) and increased infection rates (61.5%), while low motivation, burnout, and excessive workload were among the most frequently reported nurse-related barriers.Conclusion: Organizational and work-related factors, particularly excessive workload, burnout, and low motivation, were frequently perceived by nurses as barriers to the delivery of complete nursing care. Strategies to improve staffing, enhance nurses’ psychological well-being, and strengthen organizational support may reduce missed nursing care and improve patient safety and quality of care.

title: Transformational leadership and burnout among clinical healthcare workers in Inner Mongolia: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Aim To investigate the prevalence, associated factors, and model performance of burnout among clinical healthcare workers in Inner Mongolia, with particular focus on transformational leadership. Background Occupational burnout remains common among healthcare workers and may compromise workforce stability, care quality and patient safety. Transformational leadership is a potentially modifiable organizational factor that may be related to burnout, but evidence among clinical healthcare workers in resource-uneven regions remains limited. Design A cross-sectional design. Methods A convenience sample of 436 clinical healthcare workers, including 337 nurses, was recruited in Inner Mongolia between June and September 2025. Data were collected online using a general information questionnaire, the Maslach Burnout Inventory–General Survey, the short-form Perceived Organizational Support Scale, and the Transformational Leadership Questionnaire. Univariate analysis, binary logistic regression, exploratory C5.0 decision tree modeling, ROC analysis, and sensitivity analyses using both the continuous burnout score and alternative classification cut-off values were performed. Results The prevalence of burnout was 39.22% (171/436); univariate analysis identified several associated characteristics, including work experience, professional title, shift pattern and exercise frequency. Both the C5.0 and CART analyses selected transformational leadership as the first splitting variable. The C5.0 model showed a higher apparent AUC than logistic regression (0.873 vs. 0.805), but the C5.0 predictor set was derived from full-sample screening, so internal validation re-derived it within each training fold; pooled out-of-fold AUCs were 0.729 (95% CI: 0.680–0.778) for C5.0 and 0.760 (95% CI: 0.714–0.805) for logistic regression; logistic regression therefore achieved the numerically higher validated AUC, although both estimates were imprecise, were not formally compared, and equivalence or non-inferiority was not assessed. Conclusion Burnout was reported by approximately two in five of the clinical healthcare workers surveyed in Inner Mongolia, most of whom were nurses. Associated factors included work experience, professional title and perceived transformational leadership; exercise frequency was significant only for the twice-weekly category, with no dose–response pattern. Transformational leadership may represent a potentially modifiable organizational correlate of burnout, but its value as an intervention target requires confirmation through longitudinal or experimental studies.
